source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine calling and Sosthenes's shared kinship.
verses.before: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,
verses.after: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by God's will, and our brother Sosthenes,
verses.tsw_comparator: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother,

verses.rationale: Keeps location, sanctification, calling, and worldwide shared lordship.
verses.before: To the church of God that is in Corinth, to people who have been made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be a holy people, together with everyone who in every place call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ—both their Lord and ours:
verses.after: to God's church in Corinth, to those made holy in Christ Jesus and called to be saints, together with all who in every place call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ—their Lord and ours:
verses.tsw_comparator: To the church of God that is in Corinth, to those who have been made holy in Christ Jesus, called to be a holy people, together with all who in every place call upon the name of our Lord Jesus Christ—both their Lord and ours:

verses.rationale: Retains the paired greeting and both sources.
verses.before: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps thanksgiving grounded in given grace.
verses.before: I always thank my God for you, because of the grace of God that has been given to you in Christ Jesus.
verses.after: I always thank my God for you because of God's grace given to you in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: I give thanks to my God always for you, because of the grace of God that has been given to you in Christ Jesus.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated all and the two gifts.
verses.before: For in every way you have been enriched in him—in speech and knowledge of every kind—
verses.after: For in him you were enriched in every way, in all speech and all knowledge,
verses.tsw_comparator: For in every way you have been enriched in him—in speech and knowledge of every kind—

verses.rationale: Keeps the confirming relation to the community.
verses.before: just as the testimony of Christ has been confirmed among you,
verses.after: just as the testimony about Christ was confirmed among you,
verses.tsw_comparator: just as the testimony of Christ has been confirmed among you,

verses.rationale: Preserves gifted sufficiency and eschatological waiting.
verses.before: so that you are not lacking in any spiritual gift as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: so that you do not lack any gift as you eagerly await the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that you are not lacking in any spiritual gift as you wait for the revealing of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps Christ's sustaining action and final-day horizon.
verses.before: He will also strengthen you to the end, so that you may be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: He will also strengthen you to the end, blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: He will also strengthen you to the end, so that you may be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves God's faithfulness and participatory fellowship.
verses.before: God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.after: God is faithful, through whom you were called into fellowship with his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps the appeal, divisions, and paired mental unity.
verses.before: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you be in agreement, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same purpose.
verses.after: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you agree and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be restored in the same mind and the same purpose.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that all of you be in agreement, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be united in the same mind and the same purpose.

verses.rationale: Names Chloe's household as the report's source.
verses.before: For it has been reported to me by Chloe’s people that there are quarrels among you, my brothers and sisters.
verses.after: For it has been reported to me about you, my brothers and sisters, by Chloe's people, that there are quarrels among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: For it has been reported to me by Chloe’s people that there are quarrels among you, my brothers and sisters.

verses.rationale: Preserves every factional slogan.
verses.before: What I mean is this: each of you says, “I belong to Paul,” or “I belong to Apollos,” or “I belong to Cephas,” or “I belong to Christ.”
verses.after: What I mean is this: each of you says, “I belong to Paul,” “I to Apollos,” “I to Cephas,” or “I to Christ.”
verses.tsw_comparator: What I mean is this: each of you says, “I belong to Paul,” or “I belong to Apollos,” or “I belong to Cephas,” or “I belong to Christ.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the three sharp rhetorical questions.
verses.before: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
verses.after: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized into Paul's name?
verses.tsw_comparator: Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?

verses.rationale: Retains named exceptions and continuing sentence.
verses.before: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
verses.after: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,
verses.tsw_comparator: I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius,

verses.rationale: Keeps the stated anti-factional purpose.
verses.before: so that no one can say that you were baptized in my name.
verses.after: so that no one can say you were baptized into my name.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that no one can say that you were baptized in my name.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's self-correction and uncertainty.
verses.before: (I did baptize also the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.)
verses.after: I also baptized the household of Stephanas. Beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.
verses.tsw_comparator: (I did baptize also the household of Stephanas; beyond that, I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.)

verses.rationale: Keeps commission, contrast, and emptied-cross image.
verses.before: For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the good news—and not with wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.
verses.after: For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the good news—not with eloquent wisdom, so that Christ's cross would not be emptied of its power.
verses.tsw_comparator: For Christ did not send me to baptize but to proclaim the good news—and not with wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ be emptied of its power.

verses.rationale: Preserves present processes and the stark contrast.
verses.before: For the word of the cross is foolishness to people who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
verses.after: For the message of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is God's power.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps both divine actions in the quotation.
verses.before: For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the discernment of the discerning I will thwart.”
verses.after: For it is written: “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and I will reject the understanding of the intelligent.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is written, “I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the discernment of the discerning I will thwart.”

verses.rationale: Retains the rapid questions and age/world terms.
verses.before: Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?
verses.after: Where is the wise person? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has God not made the world's wisdom foolish?
verses.tsw_comparator: Where is the wise one? Where is the scribe? Where is the debater of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of the world?

verses.rationale: Preserves the wisdom wordplay and divine pleasure.
verses.before: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through wisdom, God decided, through the foolishness of what is proclaimed, to save people who believe.
verses.after: For since, in God's wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of what is proclaimed to save those who believe.
verses.tsw_comparator: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world did not know God through wisdom, God decided, through the foolishness of what is proclaimed, to save those who believe.

verses.rationale: Names both groups and their differing quests.
verses.before: For Jews demand signs and Greeks seek wisdom,
verses.after: For Jews ask for signs and Greeks seek wisdom,
verses.tsw_comparator: For Jews demand signs and Greeks seek wisdom,

verses.rationale: Keeps crucifixion and both audience reactions.
verses.before: but we proclaim Christ crucified—a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
verses.after: but we proclaim Christ crucified: a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,
verses.tsw_comparator: but we proclaim Christ crucified—a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles,

verses.rationale: Preserves common calling and repeated divine predicates.
verses.before: but to people who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
verses.after: yet to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ is God's power and God's wisdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: but to those who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the paradoxical comparative pairs.
verses.before: For God’s foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God’s weakness is stronger than human strength.
verses.after: For God's foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God's weakness is stronger than human strength.
verses.tsw_comparator: For God’s foolishness is wiser than human wisdom, and God’s weakness is stronger than human strength.

verses.rationale: Preserves social categories and repeated not many.
verses.before: Consider your own calling, brothers and sisters: not many of you were wise by human standards, not many were powerful, not many were of noble birth.
verses.after: Consider your calling, brothers and sisters: not many of you were wise by human standards, not many powerful, not many of noble birth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Consider your own calling, brothers and sisters: not many of you were wise by human standards, not many were powerful, not many were of noble birth.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine choice and both reversals.
verses.before: Yet God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;
verses.after: But God chose the foolish things of the world to shame the wise, and God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;

verses.rationale: Retains social contempt and being/nonbeing contrast.
verses.before: God chose what is low and despised in the world—things that are not—to bring to nothing things that are,
verses.after: God chose the lowborn and despised things of the world—things that are not—to bring to nothing the things that are,
verses.tsw_comparator: God chose what is low and despised in the world—things that are not—to bring to nothing things that are,

verses.rationale: Keeps the universal prohibition on boasting.
verses.before: so that no one might boast in the presence of God.
verses.after: so that no human being may boast before God.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that no one might boast in the presence of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine source and the fourfold gift.
verses.before: He is the source of your life in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,
verses.after: But it is from God that you are in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God—and righteousness, holiness, and redemption—
verses.tsw_comparator: He is the source of your life in Christ Jesus, who became for us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification and redemption,

verses.rationale: Keeps the scriptural redirection of boasting.
verses.before: so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”
verses.after: so that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
verses.tsw_comparator: in order that, as it is written, “Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's manner and the pinned testimony reading.
verses.before: I, when I came to you, brothers and sisters, did not come with superiority of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.
verses.after: And when I came to you, brothers and sisters, I did not come with superior speech or wisdom as I proclaimed God's testimony to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I, when I came to you, brothers, did not come with superiority of speech or of wisdom, proclaiming to you the testimony of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberate narrowed focus.
verses.before: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.
verses.after: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ—and him crucified.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I decided to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified.

verses.rationale: Retains all three conditions without idealizing Paul.
verses.before: I was with you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling,
verses.after: I came to you in weakness, fear, and much trembling.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I was with you in weakness and in fear and in much trembling,

verses.rationale: Keeps rhetoric/power contrast and continuing purpose.
verses.before: and my speech and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,
verses.after: My speech and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of wisdom but in a demonstration of the Spirit and power,
verses.tsw_comparator: and my speech and my proclamation were not in persuasive words of wisdom, but in demonstration of the Spirit and of power,

verses.rationale: Preserves the foundation contrast.
verses.before: so that your trust might not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.
verses.after: so that your faith would not rest on human wisdom but on God's power.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that your faith might not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps maturity, present age, and doomed rulers.
verses.before: Yet we speak wisdom among the mature, but not a wisdom of this age nor of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing;
verses.after: Yet we do speak wisdom among the mature, though not the wisdom of this age or of this age's rulers, who are passing away.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet we speak wisdom among the mature, but not a wisdom of this age nor of the rulers of this age, who are being brought to nothing;

verses.rationale: Preserves mystery, hiddenness, prior purpose, and glory.
verses.before: but we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom, which God predestined before the ages for our glory,
verses.after: Instead, we speak God's wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom God determined before the ages for our glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: but we speak God’s wisdom in a mystery, the hidden wisdom, which God predestined before the ages for our glory,

verses.rationale: Keeps rulers responsible and the striking divine title.
verses.before: which none of the rulers of this age understood; for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
verses.after: None of this age's rulers understood it, for if they had, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: which none of the rulers of this age understood; for if they had understood it, they would not have crucified the Lord of glory.

verses.rationale: Preserves the three human limits and God's preparation.
verses.before: But just as it is written, “What eye has not seen and ear has not heard, and has not entered into the heart of man, what things God has prepared for those who love him.”
verses.after: But as it is written: “What no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has imagined—what God has prepared for those who love him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But just as it is written, “What eye has not seen and ear has not heard, and has not entered into the heart of man, what things God has prepared for those who love him.”

verses.rationale: Keeps revelation and searching divine depths.
verses.before: But to us God revealed them through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches everything, even the depths of God.
verses.after: But God revealed these things to us through the Spirit, for the Spirit searches everything, even God's depths.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to us God revealed them through the Spirit; for the Spirit searches all things, even the depths of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves the human/divine analogy.
verses.before: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.
verses.after: For who among humans knows a person's thoughts except that person's spirit within? In the same way, no one knows God's thoughts except God's Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: For who among men knows the things of a man except the spirit of the man that is in him? So also no one knows the things of God except the Spirit of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps source contrast and grace-gift purpose.
verses.before: Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given to us by God,
verses.after: Now we did not receive the spirit of the world but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things God has graciously given us.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now we have received not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God, so that we may know the things freely given to us by God,

verses.rationale: Chooses a defensible reading of the compressed final phrase.
verses.before: which things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Spirit, interpreting spiritual things to spiritual people.
verses.after: We also speak these things, not in words taught by human wisdom but in words taught by the Spirit, interpreting spiritual things to spiritual people.
verses.tsw_comparator: which things we also speak, not in words taught by human wisdom, but in those taught by the Spirit, interpreting spiritual things to spiritual people.

verses.rationale: Preserves incapacity and spiritual discernment.
verses.before: But the natural person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he is not able to understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.
verses.after: But the merely natural person does not receive the things of God's Spirit, for they are foolishness to that person, who cannot understand them because they are discerned spiritually.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the natural person does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him, and he is not able to understand them, because they are spiritually discerned.

verses.rationale: Keeps the universal contrast without claiming omniscience.
verses.before: But the spiritual person discerns everything, yet he himself is discerned by no one.
verses.after: The spiritual person discerns all things but is himself judged by no one.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the spiritual person discerns all things, yet he himself is discerned by no one.

verses.rationale: Preserves quotation and communal conclusion.
verses.before: For “Who has known the mind of the Lord so as to instruct him?” But we have the mind of Christ.
verses.after: For “who has known the Lord's mind so as to instruct him?” But we have Christ's mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: For “Who has known the mind of the Lord so as to instruct him?” But we have the mind of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's direct rebuke and infancy image.
verses.before: I, brothers and sisters, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to fleshly, as to infants in Christ.
verses.after: And I, brothers and sisters, could not speak to you as spiritual people but as fleshly people, as infants in Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I, brothers, was not able to speak to you as to spiritual people, but as to fleshly, as to infants in Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves feeding metaphor and repeated inability.
verses.before: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able; but even now you are still not able,
verses.after: I fed you milk, not solid food, because you were not yet able to receive it. Even now you still are not able,
verses.tsw_comparator: I gave you milk to drink, not solid food, for you were not yet able; but even now you are still not able,

verses.rationale: Keeps evidence and rhetorical diagnosis.
verses.before: for you are still fleshly. For since there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to man?
verses.after: for you are still fleshly. Since jealousy and quarrels are among you, are you not fleshly and walking in a merely human way?
verses.tsw_comparator: for you are still fleshly. For since there is jealousy and strife among you, are you not fleshly and walking according to man?

verses.rationale: Retains factional slogans and question.
verses.before: For when one says, “I am of Paul,” and another, “I am of Apollos,” are you not merely human?
verses.after: For when one says, “I belong to Paul,” and another, “I belong to Apollos,” are you not merely human?
verses.tsw_comparator: For when one says, “I am of Paul,” and another, “I am of Apollos,” are you not merely human?

verses.rationale: Keeps leaders as instruments, not owners.
verses.before: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, as the Lord assigned to each.
verses.after: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, as the Lord assigned to each.
verses.tsw_comparator: What then is Apollos? And what is Paul? Servants through whom you believed, as the Lord assigned to each.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct work and divine agency.
verses.before: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was causing the growth.
verses.after: I planted, Apollos watered, but God caused the growth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I planted, Apollos watered, but God was causing the growth.

verses.rationale: Keeps human diminishment and divine growth.
verses.before: So then neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God who causes the growth.
verses.after: So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God who causes the growth.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but God who causes the growth.

verses.rationale: Preserves unity and individualized recompense.
verses.before: Now the one who plants and the one who waters are one, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
verses.after: The one who plants and the one who waters are one, and each will receive wages according to their own labor.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the one who plants and the one who waters are one, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three repeated God possessives.
verses.before: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.
verses.after: For we are God's coworkers; you are God's field, God's building.
verses.tsw_comparator: For we are God’s fellow workers; you are God’s field, God’s building.

verses.rationale: Preserves grace, architectural role, and warning.
verses.before: According to the grace of God given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds upon it; but let each person take care how he builds upon it.
verses.after: According to God's grace given to me, I laid a foundation like a skilled master builder, and someone else is building on it. But each person must watch how they build.
verses.tsw_comparator: According to the grace of God given to me, as a wise master builder I laid a foundation, and another builds upon it; but let each one take care how he builds upon it.

verses.rationale: Names the exclusive foundation.
verses.before: For no one can lay another foundation besides the one that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.
verses.after: For no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For no one is able to lay another foundation besides the one that is laid, which is Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps the full contrasting materials list.
verses.before: Now if someone builds upon the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,
verses.after: Now if anyone builds on the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, or straw,
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if anyone builds upon the foundation with gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, straw,

verses.rationale: Preserves Day, disclosure, fire, and testing.
verses.before: each person’s work will become evident; for the day will disclose it, because it is revealed in fire, and the fire itself will test what sort of work each person has done.
verses.after: each person's work will become evident, for the Day will disclose it. It will be revealed with fire, and the fire will test the quality of each person's work.
verses.tsw_comparator: each one’s work will become evident; for the day will disclose it, because it is revealed in fire, and the fire itself will test what sort of work each one has done.

verses.rationale: Keeps endurance and reward.
verses.before: If someone’s work which he built remains, he will receive a reward;
verses.after: If the work someone built remains, that person will receive a reward.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone’s work which he built remains, he will receive a reward;

verses.rationale: Preserves loss, salvation, and fire qualification.
verses.before: if someone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, yet so as through fire.
verses.after: If someone's work is burned up, that person will suffer loss, though personally will be saved—but only as through fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: if anyone’s work is burned up, he will suffer loss, but he himself will be saved, yet so as through fire.

verses.rationale: Makes the plural corporate referent clear.
verses.before: Do you not realize that you are God’s temple and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?
verses.after: Do you not know that you together are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells among you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know that you are God’s temple and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?

verses.rationale: Retains reciprocal destruction and corporate holiness.
verses.before: If someone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, which you are.
verses.after: If anyone destroys God's temple, God will destroy that person, for God's temple is holy—and you together are that temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone destroys God’s temple, God will destroy him; for the temple of God is holy, which you are.

verses.rationale: Keeps self-deception and wisdom reversal.
verses.before: Let no one deceive himself. If someone among you thinks that he is wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may become wise.
verses.after: Let no one deceive oneself. If anyone among you thinks they are wise in this age, let that person become foolish so as to become wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let no one deceive himself. If anyone among you thinks that he is wise in this age, let him become foolish so that he may become wise.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine evaluation and first quotation.
verses.before: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He catches the wise in their craftiness,”
verses.after: For this world's wisdom is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He catches the wise in their craftiness,”
verses.tsw_comparator: For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God. For it is written, “He catches the wise in their craftiness,”

verses.rationale: Keeps second quotation and futility.
verses.before: and again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.”
verses.after: and again, “The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and again, “The Lord knows the thoughts of the wise, that they are futile.”

verses.rationale: Connects anti-boasting to the inclusive list.
verses.before: So then let no one boast in men. For everything are yours,
verses.after: So let no one boast in human leaders, for all things are yours:
verses.tsw_comparator: So then let no one boast in men. For all things are yours,

verses.rationale: Retains every item and repeated all.
verses.before: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things present or things to come—all are yours,
verses.after: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things present or things to come—all are yours,
verses.tsw_comparator: whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas or the world or life or death or things present or things to come—all are yours,

verses.rationale: Preserves the chain of belonging.
verses.before: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.
verses.after: and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: and you are Christ’s, and Christ is God’s.

verses.rationale: Keeps subordinate service and entrusted mysteries.
verses.before: Let a person regard us in this way: as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.
verses.after: This is how people should regard us: as Christ's servants and stewards of God's mysteries.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let a person regard us in this way: as servants of Christ and stewards of the mysteries of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves stewardship criterion.
verses.before: In this case, moreover, it is required of stewards that one be found faithful.
verses.after: In this regard, what is required of stewards is that each be found faithful.
verses.tsw_comparator: In this case, moreover, it is required of stewards that one be found faithful.

verses.rationale: Keeps comparative dismissal and self-judgment limit.
verses.before: But to me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you or by any human court; in fact, I do not even judge myself.
verses.after: But to me it is a very small matter to be judged by you or by any human court. I do not even judge myself.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to me it is a very small thing that I should be judged by you or by any human court; in fact, I do not even judge myself.

verses.rationale: Preserves clear conscience without self-acquittal.
verses.before: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I am not thereby justified; but the one who judges me is the Lord.
verses.after: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I am not justified by this. The Lord is the one who judges me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am conscious of nothing against myself, but I am not thereby justified; but the one who judges me is the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps temporal restraint, disclosure, and divine praise.
verses.before: So do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and disclose the intentions of the hearts; and then each person’s praise will come from God.
verses.after: Therefore, judge nothing before the appointed time, until the Lord comes. He will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and reveal the purposes of hearts. Then each person's praise will come from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore do not judge anything before the time, until the Lord comes, who will both bring to light the hidden things of darkness and disclose the intentions of the hearts; and then each one’s praise will come from God.

verses.rationale: Preserves difficult slogan and factional purpose.
verses.before: Now these things, brothers and sisters, I have applied figuratively to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn not to go beyond what is written, so that no one of you becomes arrogant in favor of one against another.
verses.after: Now, brothers and sisters, I have applied these things to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that through us you may learn “not beyond what is written,” and so none of you becomes puffed up for one leader against another.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now these things, brothers, I have applied figuratively to myself and Apollos for your sake, so that in us you may learn not to go beyond what is written, so that no one of you becomes arrogant in favor of one against another.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three anti-boasting questions.
verses.before: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?
verses.after: For who makes you different? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why boast as though you did not?
verses.tsw_comparator: For who makes you different? And what do you have that you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as if you had not received it?

verses.rationale: Retains Paul's biting irony and wish.
verses.before: Already you are filled! Already you have become rich! You have become kings without us! And would that you had become kings, so that we also might reign with you!
verses.after: Already you are filled! Already you are rich! You have begun to reign without us! I wish you truly were reigning, so that we might reign with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Already you are filled! Already you have become rich! You have become kings without us! And would that you had become kings, so that we also might reign with you!

verses.rationale: Preserves public execution and cosmic spectacle.
verses.before: For I think that God has exhibited us apostles last of all, like men sentenced to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to men.
verses.after: For I think God has displayed us apostles last, like people sentenced to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, to angels, and to humans.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I think that God has exhibited us apostles last of all, like men sentenced to death, because we have become a spectacle to the world, both to angels and to men.

verses.rationale: Keeps the sarcastic parallel contrasts.
verses.before: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honored, but we are dishonored.
verses.after: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ! We are weak, but you are strong! You are honored, but we are dishonored!
verses.tsw_comparator: We are fools for Christ, but you are wise in Christ; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honored, but we are dishonored.

verses.rationale: Names each concrete deprivation and assault.
verses.before: To the present hour we hunger and thirst, and we are poorly clothed and are roughly treated and are homeless,
verses.after: To this very hour we are hungry and thirsty, poorly clothed, beaten, and homeless.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the present hour we hunger and thirst, and we are poorly clothed and are roughly treated and are homeless,

verses.rationale: Keeps manual labor and nonretaliatory responses.
verses.before: and we labor, working with our own hands. When reviled, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;
verses.after: We labor, working with our own hands. When insulted, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;
verses.tsw_comparator: and we labor, working with our own hands. When reviled, we bless; when persecuted, we endure;

verses.rationale: Retains degrading images without softening them.
verses.before: when slandered, we encourage. We have become like the refuse of the world, the offscouring of everything, until now.
verses.after: when slandered, we answer gently. We have become like the world's garbage, everyone's scum, to this very moment.
verses.tsw_comparator: when slandered, we encourage. We have become like the refuse of the world, the offscouring of all things, until now.

verses.rationale: Keeps purpose distinction and family affection.
verses.before: I do not write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.
verses.after: I am not writing these things to shame you but to admonish you as my beloved children.
verses.tsw_comparator: I do not write these things to shame you, but to admonish you as my beloved children.

verses.rationale: Preserves exaggerated number and paternal metaphor.
verses.before: For though you have countless instructors in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the good news.
verses.after: For even if you have ten thousand guardians in Christ, you do not have many fathers, for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though you have countless instructors in Christ, yet you do not have many fathers; for in Christ Jesus I became your father through the gospel.

verses.rationale: Keeps the direct imitation command.
verses.before: So I urge you, become imitators of me.
verses.after: Therefore, I urge you: imitate me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I urge you, become imitators of me.

verses.rationale: Preserves Timothy's relationship and consistent teaching.
verses.before: For this reason I have sent to you Timothy, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
verses.after: For this reason I sent Timothy to you, my beloved and faithful child in the Lord. He will remind you of my ways in Christ Jesus, just as I teach everywhere in every church.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this reason I have sent to you Timothy, who is my beloved and faithful child in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways in Christ, just as I teach everywhere in every church.

verses.rationale: Keeps arrogance tied to presumed absence.
verses.before: Now some have become arrogant, as if I were not coming to you;
verses.after: Some have become puffed up, as though I were not coming to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now some have become arrogant, as though I were not coming to you;

verses.rationale: Preserves divine contingency and speech/power contrast.
verses.before: but I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the speech of people who are arrogant, but their power.
verses.after: But I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the talk of those who are puffed up but their power.
verses.tsw_comparator: but I will come to you soon, if the Lord wills, and I will find out not the speech of those who are arrogant, but their power.

verses.rationale: Keeps terse kingdom contrast.
verses.before: For the kingdom of God does not consist in speech but in power.
verses.after: For God's kingdom is not a matter of talk but of power.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the kingdom of God does not consist in speech but in power.

verses.rationale: Retains disciplinary threat and gentle alternative.
verses.before: What do you want? Will I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?
verses.after: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?
verses.tsw_comparator: What do you want? Shall I come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of gentleness?

verses.rationale: Preserves the report, offense, and specific relationship.
verses.before: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such immorality as is not even among the Gentiles—that someone has his father’s wife.
verses.after: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and of a kind not tolerated even among the Gentiles: a man has his father's wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is actually reported that there is sexual immorality among you, and such immorality as is not even among the Gentiles—that someone has his father’s wife.

verses.rationale: Keeps arrogance, grief, and removal.
verses.before: And you are arrogant! Ought you not rather to mourn, so that the one who has done this deed might be removed from among you?
verses.after: And you are puffed up! Should you not instead have mourned, so that the one who did this would be removed from among you?
verses.tsw_comparator: And you are arrogant! Ought you not rather to mourn, so that the one who has done this deed might be removed from among you?

verses.rationale: Preserves absence/presence and prior judgment.
verses.before: For I indeed, though absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged the one who has done this, as if I were present:
verses.after: For though absent in body, I am present in spirit, and as though present I have already judged the one who did this.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I indeed, though absent in body but present in spirit, have already judged the one who has done this, as though I were present:

verses.rationale: Keeps communal assembly and invoked authority.
verses.before: in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are assembled, and my spirit is present, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
verses.after: When you are assembled in the name of our Lord Jesus, and I am with you in spirit, with the power of our Lord Jesus,
verses.tsw_comparator: in the name of our Lord Jesus, when you are assembled, and my spirit is present, with the power of our Lord Jesus,

verses.rationale: Retains severe discipline, bodily destruction, and saving aim.
verses.before: to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.
verses.after: hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: to deliver such a one to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps rebuke and proverbial contamination image.
verses.before: Your boasting is not good. Do you not realize that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?
verses.after: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little yeast leavens the whole batch of dough?
verses.tsw_comparator: Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?

verses.rationale: Preserves festival imagery and Christ's sacrifice.
verses.before: Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.
verses.after: Clean out the old yeast so that you may be a new batch, as you really are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Clean out the old leaven so that you may be a new lump, just as you are unleavened. For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed.

verses.rationale: Keeps sustained Passover metaphor and ethical contrasts.
verses.before: So let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
verses.after: Therefore, let us celebrate the feast not with old yeast, nor with the yeast of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let us keep the feast, not with old leaven, nor with leaven of malice and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

verses.rationale: Preserves reference to an earlier letter and continuing clarification.
verses.before: I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people—
verses.after: I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people—
verses.tsw_comparator: I wrote to you in my letter not to associate with sexually immoral people—

verses.rationale: Keeps limits and impractical consequence.
verses.before: not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would have to go out of the world.
verses.after: not at all meaning the sexually immoral people of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would have to leave the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: not at all meaning the sexually immoral of this world, or the greedy and swindlers, or idolaters, since then you would have to go out of the world.

verses.rationale: Preserves named community status and full behavior list.
verses.before: But now I write to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy or an idolater or a reviler or a drunkard or a swindler—not even to eat with such a one.
verses.after: But now I am writing to you not to associate with anyone who bears the name of brother or sister yet is sexually immoral, greedy, an idolater, verbally abusive, a drunkard, or a swindler. Do not even eat with such a person.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now I write to you not to associate with anyone who is called a brother if he is sexually immoral or greedy or an idolater or a reviler or a drunkard or a swindler—not even to eat with such a one.

verses.rationale: Keeps jurisdictional questions.
verses.before: For what have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those inside?
verses.after: For what business is it of mine to judge outsiders? Is it not those inside whom you judge?
verses.tsw_comparator: For what have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those inside?

verses.rationale: Preserves divine judgment and scriptural command.
verses.before: Yet God judges those outside. “Remove the evil person from among yourselves.”
verses.after: God judges outsiders. “Remove the evil person from among you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But God judges those outside. “Remove the evil person from among yourselves.”

verses.rationale: Keeps outrage and forum contrast.
verses.before: Does any one of you, having a matter against another, dare to go to law before the unrighteous and not before the holy ones?
verses.after: When one of you has a dispute with another, how dare you take it before the unrighteous for judgment instead of before the saints?
verses.tsw_comparator: Does any one of you, having a matter against another, dare to go to law before the unrighteous and not before the holy ones?

verses.rationale: Preserves future role and lesser-case inference.
verses.before: Or do you not realize that the holy ones will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?
verses.after: Or do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest cases?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or do you not know that the holy ones will judge the world? And if the world is judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?

verses.rationale: Keeps startling claim and inference.
verses.before: Do you not realize that we will judge angels? How much more matters of this life!
verses.after: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more the matters of this life!
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know that we will judge angels? How much more matters of this life!

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult rhetorical question and status language.
verses.before: So if you have such cases, do you appoint as judges people who are of no account in the church?
verses.after: So if you have cases concerning this life, do you appoint as judges people who have no standing in the church?
verses.tsw_comparator: So if you have such cases, do you appoint as judges those who are of no account in the church?

verses.rationale: Keeps shame and wisdom challenge.
verses.before: I say this to your shame. Is there not among you one wise man who will be able to decide between his brothers and sisters?
verses.after: I say this to your shame. Is there really no wise person among you who can decide a dispute between brothers or sisters?
verses.tsw_comparator: I say this to your shame. Is there not among you one wise man who will be able to decide between his brothers?

verses.rationale: Preserves scandal within the community.
verses.before: But brother goes to law against brother, and this before unbelievers!
verses.after: Instead, one believer goes to court against another—and before unbelievers at that!
verses.tsw_comparator: But brother goes to law against brother, and this before unbelievers!

verses.rationale: Keeps defeat and two nonretaliatory questions.
verses.before: Already then it is a defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?
verses.after: The very fact that you have lawsuits with one another is already a complete defeat for you. Why not rather suffer wrong? Why not rather be defrauded?
verses.tsw_comparator: Already then it is a defeat for you that you have lawsuits with one another. Why not rather be wronged? Why not rather be defrauded?

verses.rationale: Preserves direct accusation and harmed relationship.
verses.before: But you yourselves wrong and defraud—even your own brothers and sisters.
verses.after: But you yourselves wrong and defraud—and you do this to brothers and sisters.
verses.tsw_comparator: But you yourselves wrong and defraud—even your own brothers.

verses.rationale: Retains the warning and distinct sexual terms without euphemism.
verses.before: Or do you not realize that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor males who practice homosexuality,
verses.after: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit God's kingdom? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, idolaters, adulterers, passive male partners in sex, nor men who have sex with men,
verses.tsw_comparator: Or do you not know that the unrighteous will not inherit the kingdom of God? Do not be deceived: neither the sexually immoral, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor males who practice homosexuality,

verses.rationale: Keeps remaining behaviors and repeated outcome.
verses.before: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.
verses.after: nor thieves, the greedy, drunkards, verbal abusers, or swindlers will inherit God's kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: nor thieves, nor the greedy, nor drunkards, nor revilers, nor swindlers will inherit the kingdom of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves past identity and three passive transformations.
verses.before: And such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.
verses.after: And some of you were these things. But you were washed, you were made holy, you were declared righteous in the name of the Lord Jesus and by the Spirit of our God.
verses.tsw_comparator: And such were some of you; but you were washed, but you were sanctified, but you were justified in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and in the Spirit of our God.

verses.rationale: Treats repeated phrase as slogan and keeps mastery wordplay.
verses.before: “Everything are lawful for me,” but not everything are beneficial. “Everything are lawful for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.
verses.after: “Everything is permissible for me”—but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible for me”—but I will not be mastered by anything.
verses.tsw_comparator: “All things are lawful for me,” but not all things are beneficial. “All things are lawful for me,” but I will not be mastered by anything.

verses.rationale: Preserves slogan and bodily theological correction.
verses.before: “Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
verses.after: “Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food”—but God will bring both to an end. The body is not for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Food is for the stomach and the stomach for food,” but God will destroy both it and them. But the body is not for sexual immorality, but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

verses.rationale: Keeps past and future resurrection.
verses.before: God raised the Lord and will also raise us by his power.
verses.after: God raised the Lord and will also raise us by his power.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God raised the Lord and will also raise us by his power.

verses.rationale: Retains bodily union and emphatic rejection.
verses.before: Do you not realize that your bodies are members of Christ? Will I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!
verses.after: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take Christ's members and make them members of a prostitute? Absolutely not!
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? Shall I then take the members of Christ and make them members of a prostitute? May it never be!

verses.rationale: Preserves gendered situation and Genesis quotation.
verses.before: Or do you not realize that the one who is joined to a prostitute is one body with her? For it says, “The two will become one flesh.”
verses.after: Or do you not know that the one who joins himself to a prostitute is one body with her? For it says, “The two will become one flesh.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Or do you not know that the one who is joined to a prostitute is one body with her? For it says, “The two will become one flesh.”

verses.rationale: Keeps union contrast.
verses.before: But the one who is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.
verses.after: But the one who joins oneself to the Lord is one spirit with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the one who is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves imperative and Paul's bodily distinction.
verses.before: Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.
verses.after: Flee sexual immorality. Every other sin a person commits is outside the body, but the sexually immoral person sins against his own body.
verses.tsw_comparator: Flee sexual immorality. Every sin that a person commits is outside the body, but the one who commits sexual immorality sins against his own body.

verses.rationale: Keeps indwelling, gift, and ownership claim.
verses.before: Or do you not realize that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God, and that you are not your own?
verses.after: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God? You do not belong to yourselves,
verses.tsw_comparator: Or do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit within you, whom you have from God, and that you are not your own?

verses.rationale: Preserves purchase metaphor and embodied response.
verses.before: For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.
verses.after: for you were bought at a price. Therefore glorify God in your body.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you were bought with a price; therefore glorify God in your body.

verses.rationale: Marks the likely Corinthian slogan and its euphemism.
verses.before: Now concerning the things about which you wrote: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.
verses.after: Now concerning the matters you wrote about: “It is good for a man not to touch a woman.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now concerning the things about which you wrote: it is good for a man not to touch a woman.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal gender-specific instruction.
verses.before: But because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife and let each woman have her own husband.
verses.after: But because of sexual immorality, each man should have his own wife, and each woman her own husband.
verses.tsw_comparator: But because of sexual immoralities, let each man have his own wife and let each woman have her own husband.

verses.rationale: Preserves mutual marital obligation.
verses.before: Let the husband give to the wife her due, and likewise also the wife to the husband.
verses.after: The husband should give his wife what he owes her, and likewise the wife to her husband.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let the husband give to the wife her due, and likewise also the wife to the husband.

verses.rationale: Retains startling symmetrical authority.
verses.before: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband; and likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.
verses.after: The wife does not have authority over her own body; her husband does. Likewise, the husband does not have authority over his own body; his wife does.
verses.tsw_comparator: The wife does not have authority over her own body, but the husband; and likewise also the husband does not have authority over his own body, but the wife.

verses.rationale: Keeps consent, limited duration, prayer, reunion, and temptation.
verses.before: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer; and then come together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
verses.after: Do not deprive one another except perhaps by mutual agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer and then come together again, so Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not deprive one another, except perhaps by agreement for a time, so that you may devote yourselves to prayer; and then come together again, so that Satan may not tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's qualification.
verses.before: But this I say by way of concession, not of command.
verses.after: I say this as a concession, not as a command.
verses.tsw_comparator: But this I say by way of concession, not of command.

verses.rationale: Keeps personal preference and differing gifts.
verses.before: Yet I wish that all people were even as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that.
verses.after: I wish all people were as I am, but each has a particular gift from God, one of one kind and one of another.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet I wish that all people were even as I myself am. But each has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that.

verses.rationale: Names both groups and Paul's judgment.
verses.before: Yet I say to the unmarried and to the widows: it is good for them if they remain as I am.
verses.after: Now to the unmarried and widows I say: it is good for them to remain as I am.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to the unmarried and to the widows: it is good for them if they remain as I am.

verses.rationale: Makes the likely desire sense clear without overexplaining.
verses.before: But if they do not have self-control, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
verses.after: But if they cannot exercise self-control, they should marry, for it is better to marry than to burn with desire.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if they do not have self-control, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.

verses.rationale: Preserves authority distinction and gender-specific command.
verses.before: But to the married I give instruction—not I, but the Lord—that the wife is not to be separated from her husband
verses.after: To the married I give this command—not I, but the Lord: a wife must not separate from her husband.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the married I give instruction—not I, but the Lord—that the wife is not to be separated from her husband

verses.rationale: Keeps both alternatives and reciprocal prohibition.
verses.before: (but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband is not to divorce his wife.
verses.after: But if she does separate, she should remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And a husband must not divorce his wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: (but if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or else be reconciled to her husband), and that the husband is not to divorce his wife.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's authority qualification and the wife's consent.
verses.before: But to the rest I say—I, not the Lord—that if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, he must not divorce her.
verses.after: To the rest I say—I, not the Lord—if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, he must not divorce her.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the rest I say—I, not the Lord—that if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she consents to live with him, he must not divorce her.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal situation and consent.
verses.before: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, she must not divorce her husband.
verses.after: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, she must not divorce her husband.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if a woman has an unbelieving husband and he consents to live with her, she must not divorce her husband.

verses.rationale: Preserves relational sanctification and children's status.
verses.before: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the brother; otherwise your children are unclean, but now they are holy.
verses.after: For the unbelieving husband is made holy through his wife, and the unbelieving wife is made holy through the believing husband. Otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the unbelieving husband is sanctified in the wife, and the unbelieving wife is sanctified in the brother; otherwise your children are unclean, but now they are holy.

verses.rationale: Keeps permission, non-enslavement, and peace.
verses.before: But if the unbelieving one separates, let him separate; the brother or the sister is not enslaved in such cases, but God has called us in peace.
verses.after: But if the unbelieving partner separates, let that person separate. A brother or sister is not enslaved in such cases; God has called us to peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if the unbelieving one separates, let him separate; the brother or the sister is not enslaved in such cases, but God has called us in peace.

verses.rationale: Preserves uncertainty and reciprocal questions.
verses.before: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
verses.after: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?
verses.tsw_comparator: For how do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or how do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

verses.rationale: Keeps assigned condition, calling, and universal instruction.
verses.before: Only, as the Lord has assigned to each, as God has called each, so let him walk. And so I direct in all the churches.
verses.after: In any case, each person should live as the Lord has assigned and as God has called. This is what I direct in all the churches.
verses.tsw_comparator: Only, as the Lord has assigned to each, as God has called each, so let him walk. And so I direct in all the churches.

verses.rationale: Preserves bodily states and prohibitions.
verses.before: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.
verses.after: Was anyone already circumcised when called? He should not try to reverse it. Was anyone uncircumcised when called? He should not seek circumcision.
verses.tsw_comparator: Was anyone called having been circumcised? Let him not become uncircumcised. Has anyone been called in uncircumcision? Let him not be circumcised.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated nothing and stated priority.
verses.before: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.
verses.after: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing; what matters is keeping God's commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: Circumcision is nothing and uncircumcision is nothing, but the keeping of the commandments of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated calling language.
verses.before: Let each person remain in the calling in which he was called.
verses.after: Each person should remain in the calling in which they were called.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let each one remain in the calling in which he was called.

verses.rationale: Chooses freedom as the consequential opportunity while retaining slavery.
verses.before: Were you called as a slave? Do not let it concern you; but if indeed you can become free, rather make use of it.
verses.after: Were you enslaved when called? Do not let it trouble you. But if you can become free, make use of the opportunity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Were you called as a slave? Do not let it concern you; but if indeed you are able to become free, rather make use of it.

verses.rationale: Keeps ancient legal statuses and reversal.
verses.before: For the one called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord’s freedman; likewise, the one called as free is Christ’s slave.
verses.after: For the one who was enslaved when called in the Lord is the Lord's freed person. Likewise, the one who was free when called is Christ's slave.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the one called in the Lord as a slave is the Lord’s freedman; likewise, the one called as free is Christ’s slave.

verses.rationale: Preserves purchase and slavery imagery.
verses.before: You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.
verses.after: You were bought at a price; do not become slaves of people.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were bought with a price; do not become slaves of men.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal address and Godward setting.
verses.before: Brothers, in whatever state each was called, there let him remain with God.
verses.after: Brothers and sisters, each person should remain with God in the condition in which that person was called.
verses.tsw_comparator: Brothers, in whatever state each was called, there let him remain with God.

verses.rationale: Preserves absence of command and basis for counsel.
verses.before: Now concerning virgins I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.
verses.after: Now concerning virgins, I have no command from the Lord, but I give my judgment as one shown mercy by the Lord to be trustworthy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now concerning virgins I have no command from the Lord, but I give a judgment as one who by the Lord’s mercy is trustworthy.

verses.rationale: Keeps situational reason and qualified judgment.
verses.before: I think then that this is good because of the present distress, that it is good for a man to remain as he is.
verses.after: I think, then, because of the present crisis, that it is good for a person to remain as they are.
verses.tsw_comparator: I think then that this is good because of the present distress, that it is good for a man to remain as he is.

verses.rationale: Preserves balanced marital conditions.
verses.before: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
verses.after: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek to be released. Are you released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

verses.rationale: Keeps non-sin, concrete trouble, and pastoral aim.
verses.before: But if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have trouble in the flesh, and I would spare you.
verses.after: But if you do marry, you have not sinned, and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such people will have distress in this life, and I am trying to spare you.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you do marry, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned. Yet such will have trouble in the flesh, and I would spare you.

verses.rationale: Preserves urgency and intentionally jarring comparison.
verses.before: But this I say, brothers and sisters: the time has been shortened, so that from now on people who have wives may be as if they had none,
verses.after: This is what I mean, brothers and sisters: the time has grown short. From now on, those who have wives should live as though they had none,
verses.tsw_comparator: But this I say, brothers: the time has been shortened, so that from now on those who have wives may be as though they had none,

verses.rationale: Keeps three temporary postures.
verses.before: and people who weep as if not weeping, and people who rejoice as if not rejoicing, and people who buy as if not possessing,
verses.after: those who weep as though not weeping, those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,
verses.tsw_comparator: and those who weep as though not weeping, and those who rejoice as though not rejoicing, and those who buy as though not possessing,

verses.rationale: Preserves use/nonuse and transience.
verses.before: and people who use the world as if not using it fully; for the form of this world is passing away.
verses.after: and those who use the world as though not using it fully. For this world's present form is passing away.
verses.tsw_comparator: and those who use the world as though not using it fully; for the form of this world is passing away.

verses.rationale: Keeps stated pastoral aim and male case.
verses.before: Yet I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;
verses.after: I want you to be free from anxiety. The unmarried man is concerned about the Lord's things, how to please the Lord,
verses.tsw_comparator: But I want you to be free from concern. The unmarried man is concerned about the things of the Lord, how he may please the Lord;

verses.rationale: Preserves marital concern and continuing contrast.
verses.before: but the married man is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife,
verses.after: but the married man is concerned about worldly things, how to please his wife,
verses.tsw_comparator: but the married man is concerned about the things of the world, how he may please his wife,

verses.rationale: Keeps gender-specific parallels and whole-person holiness.
verses.before: and he is divided. And the unmarried woman and the virgin are concerned about the things of the Lord, so that they may be holy both in body and in spirit; but the married woman is concerned about the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
verses.after: and he is divided. The unmarried woman and the virgin are concerned about the Lord's things, so that they may be holy in body and spirit. But the married woman is concerned about worldly things, how to please her husband.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he is divided. And the unmarried woman and the virgin are concerned about the things of the Lord, so that they may be holy both in body and in spirit; but the married woman is concerned about the things of the world, how she may please her husband.

verses.rationale: Preserves benefit, noose image's restraint sense, and devotion.
verses.before: And this I say for your own benefit, not to put a restraint upon you, but for what is proper and to promote undivided devotion to the Lord.
verses.after: I say this for your own benefit, not to put a restraint around you, but to promote good order and undistracted devotion to the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this I say for your own benefit, not to put a restraint upon you, but for what is proper and to promote undivided devotion to the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves interpretive ambiguity around the man's relation while stating marriage outcome.
verses.before: But if someone thinks he is acting improperly toward his virgin, if she is past her youth and it must be so, let him do what he wishes; he does not sin—let them marry.
verses.after: But if anyone thinks he is behaving improperly toward his virgin, if she is past marriageable age and it ought to be so, he should do what he wants; he is not sinning. They should marry.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if anyone thinks he is acting improperly toward his virgin, if she is past her youth and it must be so, let him do what he wishes; he does not sin—let them marry.

verses.rationale: Keeps internal resolve, freedom, and debated relationship.
verses.before: But the one who stands firm in his heart, having no necessity, but having authority over his own will, and has determined this in his heart, to keep his virgin, he will do well.
verses.after: But the man who stands firm in his heart, under no compulsion and having control over his own will, and has decided in his heart to keep his virgin unmarried, will do well.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the one who stands firm in his heart, having no necessity, but having authority over his own will, and has determined this in his heart, to keep his virgin, he will do well.

verses.rationale: Preserves comparative counsel without turning it into command.
verses.before: So then both the one who gives his virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage will do better.
verses.after: So the one who marries his virgin does well, and the one who does not marry will do better.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then both the one who gives his virgin in marriage does well, and the one who does not give her in marriage will do better.

verses.rationale: Keeps duration, death euphemism, freedom, and qualification.
verses.before: A wife is bound as long as her husband lives; but if the husband dies, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord.
verses.after: A wife is bound as long as her husband lives. But if her husband falls asleep in death, she is free to marry anyone she wishes, only in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: A wife is bound as long as her husband lives; but if the husband dies, she is free to be married to whom she wishes, only in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's counsel and gently ironic authority claim.
verses.before: But in my judgment she is happier if she remains as she is—and I think that I also have the Spirit of God.
verses.after: Yet in my judgment she is happier if she remains as she is—and I think that I too have God's Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in my judgment she is happier if she remains as she is—and I think that I also have the Spirit of God.

verses.rationale: Marks slogan and preserves inflate/build contrast.
verses.before: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
verses.after: Now concerning food sacrificed to idols: we know that “we all have knowledge.” Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now concerning things sacrificed to idols: we know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.

verses.rationale: Keeps epistemic humility.
verses.before: If someone thinks that he knows anything, he does not yet know as he ought to know;
verses.after: If anyone thinks they know something, they do not yet know as they ought to know.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone thinks that he knows anything, he does not yet know as he ought to know;

verses.rationale: Preserves divine knowing as decisive.
verses.before: but if someone loves God, he is known by him.
verses.after: But if anyone loves God, that person is known by God.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if anyone loves God, he is known by him.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired confessional claims as likely slogans.
verses.before: So concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God except one.
verses.after: So concerning the eating of food sacrificed to idols, we know that “an idol is nothing in the world” and that “there is no God but one.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore concerning the eating of things sacrificed to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world and that there is no God except one.

verses.rationale: Preserves concession and ancient plural claims.
verses.before: For even if there are so-called gods whether in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many gods and many lords—
verses.after: For even if there are so-called gods, whether in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many gods and many lords—
verses.tsw_comparator: For even if there are so-called gods whether in heaven or on earth—as indeed there are many gods and many lords—

verses.rationale: Keeps one-God confession and distinct prepositions.
verses.before: yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are everything and we for him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are everything and we through him.
verses.after: yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and for whom we exist; and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and through whom we exist.
verses.tsw_comparator: yet for us there is one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we for him, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom are all things and we through him.

verses.rationale: Preserves prior formation, eating, weakness, and defilement.
