verses.before: However, not all have this knowledge; but some, being accustomed to the idol until now, eat food as something sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
verses.after: But not everyone has this knowledge. Some, through their former association with the idol, still eat food as truly offered to an idol, and their weak conscience is defiled.
verses.tsw_comparator: However, not all have this knowledge; but some, being accustomed to the idol until now, eat food as something sacrificed to an idol, and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.

verses.rationale: Keeps the balanced lack of spiritual advantage.
verses.before: But food will not commend us to God; neither if we do not eat are we worse, nor if we eat are we better.
verses.after: Food will not bring us before God. We are no worse if we do not eat and no better if we do.
verses.tsw_comparator: But food will not commend us to God; neither if we do not eat are we worse, nor if we eat are we better.

verses.rationale: Preserves liberty and harm warning.
verses.before: But take care that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.
verses.after: But take care that this freedom of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.
verses.tsw_comparator: But take care that this right of yours does not somehow become a stumbling block to the weak.

verses.rationale: Keeps temple setting and dangerous encouragement.
verses.before: For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, if he is weak, be built up to eat things sacrificed to idols?
verses.after: For if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining to eat in an idol's temple, will not that person's weak conscience be encouraged to eat food sacrificed to idols?
verses.tsw_comparator: For if anyone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining in an idol’s temple, will not his conscience, if he is weak, be built up to eat things sacrificed to idols?

verses.rationale: Preserves grave consequence and Christ's death.
verses.before: For through your knowledge the weak one is destroyed—the brother for whom Christ died.
verses.after: So by your knowledge the weak person is destroyed—the brother or sister for whom Christ died.
verses.tsw_comparator: For through your knowledge the weak one is destroyed—the brother for whom Christ died.

verses.rationale: Keeps bodily striking metaphor as wound and Christward offense.
verses.before: And thus, sinning against the brothers and sisters and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
verses.after: When you sin in this way against brothers and sisters and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: And thus, sinning against the brothers and wounding their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's absolute self-limitation.
verses.before: So, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat forever, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.
verses.after: Therefore, if food causes my brother or sister to stumble, I will never eat meat again, so that I do not cause them to stumble.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, if food causes my brother to stumble, I will never eat meat forever, so that I may not cause my brother to stumble.

verses.rationale: Keeps all four credentials as questions.
verses.before: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
verses.after: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?
verses.tsw_comparator: Am I not free? Am I not an apostle? Have I not seen Jesus our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

verses.rationale: Preserves community as validating seal.
verses.before: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
verses.after: If I am not an apostle to others, at least I am to you, for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: If to others I am not an apostle, yet at least I am to you; for you are the seal of my apostleship in the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps courtroom language and concise transition.
verses.before: My defense to people who examine me is this:
verses.after: This is my defense to those who examine me.
verses.tsw_comparator: My defense to those who examine me is this:

verses.rationale: Preserves apostolic entitlement question.
verses.before: Do we not have the right to eat and drink?
verses.after: Do we not have the right to eat and drink?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do we not have the right to eat and drink?

verses.rationale: Keeps gender, marriage, and named comparators.
verses.before: Do we not have the right to take along a believing wife, as also the other apostles and the brothers and sisters of the Lord and Cephas?
verses.after: Do we not have the right to take along a believing wife, as do the other apostles, the Lord's brothers, and Cephas?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do we not have the right to take along a believing wife, as also the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas?

verses.rationale: Names Barnabas and clarifies the labor issue.
verses.before: Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to refrain from working?
verses.after: Or are Barnabas and I the only ones who have no right to refrain from working for a living?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or is it only Barnabas and I who have no right to refrain from working?

verses.rationale: Preserves three occupational analogies.
verses.before: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not drink from the milk of the flock?
verses.after: Who ever serves as a soldier at their own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who tends a flock and does not drink its milk?
verses.tsw_comparator: Who serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Or who shepherds a flock and does not drink from the milk of the flock?

verses.rationale: Keeps two-source rhetorical progression.
verses.before: Am I speaking these things according to human judgment, or does not the law also say these things?
verses.after: Am I saying these things merely on human authority? Does not the law also say them?
verses.tsw_comparator: Am I speaking these things according to human judgment, or does not the law also say these things?

verses.rationale: Preserves law attribution, animal care, and question.
verses.before: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You will not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is God concerned about oxen?
verses.after: For in Moses's law it is written, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is threshing grain.” Is God concerned only about oxen?
verses.tsw_comparator: For it is written in the law of Moses, “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.” Is God concerned about oxen?

verses.rationale: Keeps application and repeated hope.
verses.before: Or is he speaking altogether for our sake? Yes, for our sake it was written, because the one who plows ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes in hope of sharing.
verses.after: Or is he certainly speaking for our sake? Yes, it was written for us, because the plowman should plow in hope and the thresher thresh in hope of sharing the harvest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Or is he speaking altogether for our sake? Yes, for our sake it was written, because the one who plows ought to plow in hope, and the one who threshes in hope of sharing.

verses.rationale: Preserves sow/reap and spiritual/material contrast.
verses.before: If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?
verses.after: If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material support from you?
verses.tsw_comparator: If we sowed spiritual things among you, is it too much if we reap material things from you?

verses.rationale: Keeps renounced right and gospel purpose.
verses.before: If others share this right over you, do we not more? But we did not use this right, but we endure everything so that we may not put any obstacle in the way of the good news of Christ.
verses.after: If others share this right over you, do we not have it even more? Yet we have not used this right. Instead, we endure everything so that we may place no obstacle in Christ's good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: If others share this right over you, do we not more? But we did not use this right, but we endure all things so that we may not put any obstacle in the way of the gospel of Christ.

verses.rationale: Preserves temple and altar analogies.
verses.before: Do you not realize that people who perform sacred services eat the things of the temple, and people who attend the altar share with the altar?
verses.after: Do you not know that those who work in the temple eat food from the temple, and those who serve at the altar share in what is offered on the altar?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know that those who perform sacred services eat the things of the temple, and those who attend the altar share with the altar?

verses.rationale: Keeps divine command and repeated gospel.
verses.before: So also the Lord directed people who proclaim the good news to live from the good news.
verses.after: In the same way, the Lord commanded that those who proclaim the good news should live from the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also the Lord directed those who proclaim the gospel to live from the gospel.

verses.rationale: Retains Paul's broken sentence and vehement boast.
verses.before: Yet I have used none of these things, and I am not writing these things so that it will be done for me; for it would be better for me to die than—no one will empty my boast!
verses.after: But I have used none of these rights. And I am not writing this so that they will be granted to me. I would rather die than—no one will empty my reason for boasting!
verses.tsw_comparator: But I have used none of these things, and I am not writing these things so that it will be done for me; for it would be better for me to die than—no one will empty my boast!

verses.rationale: Keeps compulsion and prophetic woe.
verses.before: For if I proclaim the good news, I have nothing to boast of, for necessity is laid upon me; for woe to me if I do not proclaim the good news!
verses.after: For if I proclaim the good news, I have no reason to boast, since necessity is laid on me. Woe to me if I do not proclaim the good news!
verses.tsw_comparator: For if I proclaim the gospel, I have nothing to boast of, for necessity is laid upon me; for woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!

verses.rationale: Preserves willing/unwilling and entrusted office.
verses.before: For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I am entrusted with a stewardship.
verses.after: For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I have still been entrusted with a stewardship.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if unwillingly, I am entrusted with a stewardship.

verses.rationale: Keeps reward as relinquished entitlement.
verses.before: What then is my reward? That when I proclaim the good news, I may offer the good news free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the good news.
verses.after: What then is my reward? That in proclaiming the good news I may offer it free of charge and not make full use of my right in the good news.
verses.tsw_comparator: What then is my reward? That when I proclaim the gospel, I may offer the gospel free of charge, so as not to make full use of my right in the gospel.

verses.rationale: Preserves freedom/slavery reversal and mission aim.
verses.before: For though I am free from all, I have made myself a slave to all, so that I may win more.
verses.after: For though I am free from everyone, I made myself a slave to everyone in order to win more people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For though I am free from all, I have made myself a slave to all, so that I may win more.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jewish identity rhetoric and pinned qualification.
verses.before: And to the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews; to those under the law, as under the law (though not being myself under the law), so that I might win those under the law;
verses.after: To the Jews I became like a Jew, to win Jews. To those under the law I became like one under the law—though I myself am not under the law—to win those under the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: And to the Jews I became as a Jew, so that I might win Jews; to those under the law, as under the law (though not being myself under the law), so that I might win those under the law;

verses.rationale: Preserves double legal qualification.
verses.before: to those without the law, as without the law (though not being without law toward God but under the law of Christ), so that I might win those without the law.
verses.after: To those outside the law I became like one outside the law—though I am not outside God's law but under Christ's law—to win those outside the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: to those without the law, as without the law (though not being without law toward God but under the law of Christ), so that I might win those without the law.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated weak, expansive adaptation, and limited some.
verses.before: To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become everything to all people, so that by all means I might save some.
verses.after: To the weak I became weak, to win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by every possible means I might save some.
verses.tsw_comparator: To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, so that by all means I might save some.

verses.rationale: Preserves participation as Paul's aim.
verses.before: I do everything for the sake of the good news, so that I may become a fellow partaker of it.
verses.after: I do all this for the sake of the good news, so that I may share in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I do all things for the sake of the gospel, so that I may become a fellow partaker of it.

verses.rationale: Keeps athletic setting and imperative.
verses.before: Do you not realize that people who run in a race all run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.
verses.after: Do you not know that all the runners in a stadium run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may win it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do you not know that those who run in a race all run, but only one receives the prize? Run in such a way that you may obtain it.

verses.rationale: Preserves discipline and two crowns.
verses.before: And everyone who competes exercises self-control in everything; they then do it to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable.
verses.after: Every athlete exercises self-control in everything. They do it to receive a perishable wreath, but we an imperishable one.
verses.tsw_comparator: And everyone who competes exercises self-control in all things; they then do it to receive a perishable crown, but we an imperishable.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired athletic metaphors.
verses.before: So I run in this way, not as uncertainly; I box in this way, not as beating the air;
verses.after: So I do not run aimlessly or box as one beating the air.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I run in this way, not as uncertainly; I box in this way, not as beating the air;

verses.rationale: Retains harsh bodily discipline and disqualification risk.
verses.before: but I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest after proclaiming to others, I myself should become disqualified.
verses.after: Instead, I strike my body and make it my slave, so that after proclaiming to others I myself will not be disqualified.
verses.tsw_comparator: but I discipline my body and bring it into subjection, lest after proclaiming to others, I myself should become disqualified.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared ancestry and repeated all.
verses.before: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,
verses.after: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers and sisters, that our ancestors were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, that our fathers were all under the cloud and all passed through the sea,

verses.rationale: Preserves unusual baptismal analogy.
verses.before: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
verses.after: They were all baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated all and continuing thought.
verses.before: and all ate the same spiritual food,
verses.after: They all ate the same spiritual food,
verses.tsw_comparator: and all ate the same spiritual food,

verses.rationale: Preserves following-rock tradition and christological identification.
verses.before: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they were drinking from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.
verses.after: and all drank the same spiritual drink. For they drank from the spiritual rock that followed them, and that rock was Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all drank the same spiritual drink; for they were drinking from a spiritual rock that followed them, and the rock was Christ.

verses.rationale: Retains divine displeasure and corpses in desert.
verses.before: But with most of them God was not pleased, for they were struck down in the wilderness.
verses.after: Nevertheless, God was not pleased with most of them, and their bodies were scattered across the wilderness.
verses.tsw_comparator: But with most of them God was not pleased, for they were struck down in the wilderness.

verses.rationale: Keeps typological warning and desire.
verses.before: Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.
verses.after: Now these things became examples for us, so that we would not desire evil things as they did.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now these things became examples for us, so that we might not desire evil things as they also desired.

verses.rationale: Preserves command and quoted scene.
verses.before: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were; just as it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”
verses.after: Do not become idolaters as some of them did, as it is written: “The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be idolaters, as some of them were; just as it is written, “The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.”

verses.rationale: Keeps exact number and fatal consequence.
verses.before: Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and fell in one day twenty-three thousand.
verses.after: Let us not commit sexual immorality as some of them did, and twenty-three thousand fell in one day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nor let us commit sexual immorality, as some of them committed, and fell in one day twenty-three thousand.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned Christ reading and physical deaths.
verses.before: Nor let us test Christ, as some of them tested and were destroyed by serpents.
verses.after: Let us not test Christ as some of them did and were destroyed by snakes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nor let us test Christ, as some of them tested and were destroyed by serpents.

verses.rationale: Keeps grumbling and destructive agent.
verses.before: Nor grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.
verses.after: And do not grumble as some of them did and were destroyed by the destroyer.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nor grumble, as some of them grumbled and were destroyed by the destroyer.

verses.rationale: Preserves typology, writing, and eschatological arrival.
verses.before: Now these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our instruction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.
verses.after: These things happened to them as examples and were written as a warning for us, on whom the ends of the ages have come.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now these things happened to them as examples, and they were written for our instruction, upon whom the ends of the ages have come.

verses.rationale: Keeps stand/fall warning.
verses.before: So let the one who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.
verses.after: So the one who thinks they stand must watch out lest they fall.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let the one who thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.

verses.rationale: Preserves both testing/trial senses and promise of endurance.
verses.before: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also provide the way of escape, so that you may be able to endure it.
verses.after: No trial has overtaken you except what is common to humanity. God is faithful; he will not allow you to be tested beyond what you can bear, but with the trial he will also provide a way out so that you can endure it.
verses.tsw_comparator: No temptation has overtaken you except what is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also provide the way of escape, so that you may be able to endure it.

verses.rationale: Keeps affectionate direct command.
verses.before: So, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
verses.after: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.

verses.rationale: Preserves appeal to discernment.
verses.before: I speak as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.
verses.after: I speak to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.
verses.tsw_comparator: I speak as to sensible people; judge for yourselves what I say.

verses.rationale: Keeps ritual actions and repeated participation.
verses.before: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a participation in the body of Christ?
verses.after: The cup of blessing that we bless—is it not participation in Christ's blood? The bread that we break—is it not participation in Christ's body?
verses.tsw_comparator: The cup of blessing that we bless, is it not a participation in the blood of Christ? The bread that we break, is it not a participation in the body of Christ?

verses.rationale: Preserves bread/body unity and all.
verses.before: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one bread.
verses.after: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for all of us partake of the one bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body; for we all partake of the one bread.

verses.rationale: Keeps Israel designation and cultic participation.
verses.before: Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not people who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?
verses.after: Consider Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?
verses.tsw_comparator: Look at Israel according to the flesh: are not those who eat the sacrifices participants in the altar?

verses.rationale: Keeps two denying questions.
verses.before: What then do I say? That what is sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
verses.after: What then am I saying? That food sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?
verses.tsw_comparator: What then do I say? That what is sacrificed to an idol is anything, or that an idol is anything?

verses.rationale: Preserves demonic referent and participation warning.
verses.before: No, but that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to become participants with demons.
verses.after: No, but what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. I do not want you to become participants with demons.
verses.tsw_comparator: No, but that what they sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God; and I do not want you to become participants with demons.

verses.rationale: Keeps paired exclusive tables.
verses.before: You are not able to drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you are not able to partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.
verses.after: You cannot drink the Lord's cup and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the Lord's table and the table of demons.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are not able to drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons; you are not able to partake of the table of the Lord and the table of demons.

verses.rationale: Preserves covenantal jealousy and challenge.
verses.before: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
verses.after: Or are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he is?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or do we provoke the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?

verses.rationale: Marks repeated slogan and two tests.
verses.before: “Everything are lawful,” but not everything are beneficial. “Everything are lawful,” but not everything build up.
verses.after: “Everything is permissible,” but not everything is beneficial. “Everything is permissible,” but not everything builds up.
verses.tsw_comparator: “All things are lawful,” but not all things are beneficial. “All things are lawful,” but not all things build up.

verses.rationale: Keeps self/other contrast.
verses.before: Let no one seek his own good, but that of the other.
verses.after: No one should seek one's own good but the good of the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let no one seek his own good, but that of the other.

verses.rationale: Preserves market freedom and conscience reason.
verses.before: Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, asking no questions for conscience’ sake;
verses.after: Eat anything sold in the meat market without raising questions for conscience's sake,
verses.tsw_comparator: Eat whatever is sold in the meat market, asking no questions for conscience’ sake;

verses.rationale: Keeps scriptural ownership ground.
verses.before: for “the earth is the Lord’s and the fullness thereof.”
verses.after: for “the earth is the Lord's, and everything in it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for “the earth is the Lord’s and the fullness thereof.”

verses.rationale: Preserves voluntary visit and ordinary hospitality.
verses.before: If one of the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for conscience’ sake.
verses.after: If an unbeliever invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you without raising questions for conscience's sake.
verses.tsw_comparator: If one of the unbelievers invites you and you wish to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for conscience’ sake.

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit disclosure and relational restraint.
verses.before: But if someone says to you, “This has been offered in sacrifice,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for conscience’ sake—
verses.after: But if someone tells you, “This was offered in sacrifice,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for conscience's sake—
verses.tsw_comparator: But if someone says to you, “This has been offered in sacrifice,” do not eat it, for the sake of the one who informed you and for conscience’ sake—

verses.rationale: Clarifies referent and preserves question.
verses.before: not your own conscience, but that of the other. For why is my freedom judged by another’s conscience?
verses.after: I mean the other person's conscience, not your own. For why should my freedom be judged by someone else's conscience?
verses.tsw_comparator: not your own conscience, but that of the other. For why is my freedom judged by another’s conscience?

verses.rationale: Keeps grace/gratitude and public criticism.
verses.before: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I spoken against for that for which I give thanks?
verses.after: If I partake with gratitude, why am I denounced for something for which I give thanks?
verses.tsw_comparator: If I partake with thankfulness, why am I spoken against for that for which I give thanks?

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive scope and purpose.
verses.before: So, whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
verses.after: So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do everything for God's glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.

verses.rationale: Names all three groups.
verses.before: Give no offense either to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God,
verses.after: Give no offense to Jews, Greeks, or God's church,
verses.tsw_comparator: Give no offense either to Jews or to Greeks or to the church of God,

verses.rationale: Keeps accommodation, self-denial, and saving purpose.
verses.before: just as I also please all people in everything, not seeking my own advantage, but that of the many, so that they may be saved.
verses.after: just as I try to please everyone in everything, not seeking my own advantage but that of the many, so that they may be saved.
verses.tsw_comparator: just as I also please all people in all things, not seeking my own advantage, but that of the many, so that they may be saved.

verses.rationale: Preserves qualified imitation.
verses.before: Be imitators of me, just as I also am of Christ.
verses.after: Imitate me, just as I imitate Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be imitators of me, just as I also am of Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps praise, memory, and transmitted practices.
verses.before: Now I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold firmly to the traditions, just as I delivered them to you.
verses.after: Now I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold firmly to the traditions just as I delivered them to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I praise you because you remember me in everything and hold firmly to the traditions, just as I delivered them to you.

verses.rationale: Retains gendered sequence and ambiguous head metaphor.
verses.before: Yet I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.
verses.after: But I want you to know that Christ is the head of every man, the man is the head of a woman, and God is the head of Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I want you to understand that the head of every man is Christ, the head of a woman is the man, and the head of Christ is God.

verses.rationale: Preserves male worship activity and disputed covering description.
verses.before: Every man who prays or prophesies with something on his head disgraces his head.
verses.after: Every man who prays or prophesies with something hanging down from his head dishonors his head.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every man who prays or prophesies with something on his head disgraces his head.

verses.rationale: Keeps women's active worship and shame comparison.
verses.before: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disgraces her head—it is one and the same as if her head were shaved.
verses.after: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered dishonors her head, for it is one and the same as having her head shaved.
verses.tsw_comparator: But every woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disgraces her head—it is one and the same as if her head were shaved.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's conditional cultural reasoning.
verses.before: For if a woman does not cover her head, she might as well have her hair cut off; but if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, let her cover her head.
verses.after: For if a woman does not cover her head, she should also have her hair cut off. But if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved, she should cover her head.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if a woman does not cover her head, she might as well have her hair cut off; but if it is shameful for a woman to have her hair cut off or be shaved, let her cover her head.

verses.rationale: Retains gender-specific claims without smoothing them.
verses.before: For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.
verses.after: For a man ought not cover his head, since he is God's image and glory, but woman is man's glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: For a man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God; but woman is the glory of man.

verses.rationale: Keeps creation-order argument.
verses.before: For man was not made from woman, but woman from man.
verses.after: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man;
verses.tsw_comparator: For man was not made from woman, but woman from man.

verses.rationale: Preserves stated purpose relation.
verses.before: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.
verses.after: and man was not created for woman, but woman for man.
verses.tsw_comparator: Neither was man created for woman, but woman for man.

verses.rationale: Renders authority positively and retains angelic rationale.
verses.before: For this reason a woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.
verses.after: For this reason, and because of the angels, a woman ought to have authority over her head.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this reason a woman ought to have authority over her head, because of the angels.

verses.rationale: Keeps mutual dependence as qualification.
verses.before: Even so, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man independent of woman.
verses.after: Nevertheless, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man independent of woman.
verses.tsw_comparator: Nevertheless, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor man independent of woman.

verses.rationale: Preserves origin reversal and divine source.
verses.before: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born through woman—and everything are from God.
verses.after: For just as woman came from man, so man is born through woman, and all things come from God.
verses.tsw_comparator: For just as woman came from man, so also man is born through woman—and all things are from God.

verses.rationale: Keeps appeal and gendered question.
verses.before: Judge for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
verses.after: Judge for yourselves: is it fitting for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?
verses.tsw_comparator: Judge for yourselves: is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's nature claim and continuing contrast.
verses.before: Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair it is a dishonor to him,
verses.after: Does not nature itself teach you that if a man wears long hair, it is a dishonor to him,
verses.tsw_comparator: Does not even nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair it is a dishonor to him,

verses.rationale: Keeps hair/glory/covering relation.
verses.before: but if a woman has long hair it is her glory? For her hair is given to her for a covering.
verses.after: but if a woman wears long hair, it is her glory? For her hair is given to her as a covering.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if a woman has long hair it is her glory? For her hair is given to her for a covering.

verses.rationale: Preserves dispute-closing appeal to communal practice.
verses.before: But if someone is inclined to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.
verses.after: But if anyone is inclined to be contentious, we have no other practice, nor do God's churches.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if anyone is inclined to be contentious, we have no such custom, nor do the churches of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit blame and harmful assembly.
verses.before: But in giving this instruction I do not praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.
verses.after: Now in giving this instruction, I do not praise you, because when you gather it is not for the better but for the worse.
verses.tsw_comparator: But in giving this instruction I do not praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.

verses.rationale: Preserves report and qualified belief.
verses.before: For in the first place, when you come together as a church, I hear that there are divisions among you; and in part I trust it,
verses.after: For first, when you gather as a church, I hear there are divisions among you, and to some extent I believe it.
verses.tsw_comparator: For in the first place, when you come together as a church, I hear that there are divisions among you; and in part I trust it,

verses.rationale: Keeps necessity and revealing function.
verses.before: for there must also be factions among you, so that people who are approved may become evident among you.
verses.after: Indeed, factions must also arise among you so that those who are approved may become evident among you.
verses.tsw_comparator: for there must also be factions among you, so that those who are approved may become evident among you.

verses.rationale: Preserves ironic negation of their meal.
verses.before: When you come together, it is not to eat the Lord’s supper,
verses.after: So when you gather in the same place, it is not really the Lord's supper you eat.
verses.tsw_comparator: When you come together, it is not to eat the Lord’s supper,

verses.rationale: Names inequity, hunger, and drunkenness.
verses.before: for in eating, each person goes ahead with their own meal, and one is hungry while another is drunk.
verses.after: For in eating, each person goes ahead with their own supper; one goes hungry while another gets drunk.
verses.tsw_comparator: for in eating, each one goes ahead with their own meal, and one is hungry while another is drunk.

verses.rationale: Keeps socioeconomic harm and repeated refusal to praise.
verses.before: What! Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and shame people who have nothing? What will I say to you? Will I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
verses.after: Do you not have houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise God's church and humiliate those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.
verses.tsw_comparator: What! Do you not have houses to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you.

verses.rationale: Preserves receive/hand on/handed over word connections.
verses.before: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when he was betrayed, took bread,
verses.after: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you: the Lord Jesus, on the night when he was handed over, took bread,
verses.tsw_comparator: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you: that the Lord Jesus, on the night when he was betrayed, took bread,

verses.rationale: Follows pinned text without an added broken phrase.
verses.before: and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
verses.after: and after giving thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant, blood, repetition, and remembrance.
verses.before: In the same way also the cup, after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.”
verses.after: In the same way, after supper he took the cup, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Whenever you drink it, do this in remembrance of me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: In the same way also the cup, after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves proclamation between death and coming.
verses.before: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
verses.after: For whenever you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

verses.rationale: Keeps manner, alternative or, and grave accountability.
verses.before: So, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be accountable for the body and blood of the Lord.
verses.after: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the Lord's cup in an unworthy manner will be answerable for the Lord's body and blood.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be accountable for the body and blood of the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves self-examination leading to participation.
verses.before: Let a person examine themselves, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup.
verses.after: A person should examine oneself, and in this way eat from the bread and drink from the cup.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let a person examine themselves, and so eat of the bread and drink of the cup.

verses.rationale: Keeps body ambiguity and self-incurred judgment.
verses.before: For anyone who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on themselves.
verses.after: For the one who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on oneself.
verses.tsw_comparator: For anyone who eats and drinks without discerning the body eats and drinks judgment on themselves.

verses.rationale: Retains claimed consequence and death euphemism.
verses.before: For this reason many among you are weak and ill, and some have died.
verses.after: That is why many among you are weak and sick, and quite a few have fallen asleep in death.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this reason many among you are weak and ill, and some have died.

verses.rationale: Keeps discern/judge wordplay.
verses.before: But if we were judging ourselves, we would not be judged.
verses.after: But if we discerned ourselves, we would not be judged.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if we were judging ourselves, we would not be judged.

verses.rationale: Preserves corrective purpose and final contrast.
verses.before: Yet when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned along with the world.
verses.after: Yet when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we will not be condemned with the world.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned along with the world.

verses.rationale: Keeps communal solution.
verses.before: So then, my sisters and brothers and sisters, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
verses.after: Therefore, my brothers and sisters, when you gather to eat, wait for one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then, my sisters and brothers, when you come together to eat, wait for one another.

verses.rationale: Preserves practical instruction and deferred orders.
verses.before: If someone is hungry, let them eat at home, so that when you come together it will not be for judgment. And the rest I will set in order when I come.
verses.after: If anyone is hungry, that person should eat at home, so that your gathering does not result in judgment. I will arrange the remaining matters when I come.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone is hungry, let them eat at home, so that when you come together it will not be for judgment. And the rest I will set in order when I come.

verses.rationale: Uses gifts while noting the Greek's broader spiritual-things sense.
verses.before: Now concerning spiritual matters, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be uninformed.
verses.after: Now concerning spiritual gifts, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be uninformed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now concerning spiritual matters, brothers and sisters, I do not want you to be uninformed.

verses.rationale: Keeps former identity and passive misdirection.
verses.before: You know that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.
verses.after: You know that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.
verses.tsw_comparator: You know that when you were Gentiles, you were led astray to mute idols, however you were led.

verses.rationale: Preserves two confessions and Spirit criterion.
verses.before: So I reveal to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says, “Jesus is accursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except in the Holy Spirit.
verses.after: Therefore, I want you to know that no one speaking by God's Spirit says, “Jesus is accursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except by the Holy Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore I make known to you that no one speaking in the Spirit of God says, “Jesus is accursed,” and no one can say, “Jesus is Lord,” except in the Holy Spirit.

verses.rationale: Keeps diversity/unity refrain.
verses.before: Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit;
verses.after: There are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit;
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit;

verses.rationale: Preserves parallel service language.
verses.before: and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord;
verses.after: there are varieties of ministries, but the same Lord;
verses.tsw_comparator: and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord;

verses.rationale: Keeps divine working and repeated all.
verses.before: and there are varieties of workings, but the same God who works everything in all.
verses.after: and there are varieties of activities, but the same God activates all of them in everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: and there are varieties of workings, but the same God who works all things in all.

verses.rationale: Preserves individual gift and communal purpose.
verses.before: To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.
verses.after: A manifestation of the Spirit is given to each person for the common good.
verses.tsw_comparator: To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common good.

verses.rationale: Keeps distinct speech gifts and same Spirit.
verses.before: For to one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,
verses.after: To one is given through the Spirit a message of wisdom, and to another a message of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
verses.tsw_comparator: For to one is given through the Spirit a word of wisdom, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit,

verses.rationale: Preserves faith and plural healings.
verses.before: to another faith in the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings in the one Spirit,
verses.after: to another faith by the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healing by the one Spirit;
verses.tsw_comparator: to another faith in the same Spirit, to another gifts of healings in the one Spirit,

verses.rationale: Keeps the full differentiated list.
verses.before: to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another discernments of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues.
verses.after: to another workings of miracles, to another prophecy, to another discernment of spirits, to another various kinds of tongues, and to another interpretation of tongues.
verses.tsw_comparator: to another workings of powers, to another prophecy, to another discernments of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, to another interpretation of tongues.

verses.rationale: Preserves Spirit's agency and will.
verses.before: All these are worked by the one and the same Spirit, distributing to each person individually just as he wills.
verses.after: One and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each person individually just as the Spirit wills.
verses.tsw_comparator: All these are worked by the one and the same Spirit, distributing to each one individually just as he wills.

verses.rationale: Keeps one/many repetition and identifies Christ with body.
verses.before: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so also Christ.
verses.after: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the body's members, though many, are one body, so also is Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: For just as the body is one and has many members, and all the members of the body, though many, are one body, so also Christ.

verses.rationale: Retains ethnic and status pairs, including slavery.
verses.before: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free—and all were made to drink of one Spirit.
verses.after: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, enslaved or free—and we were all given one Spirit to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: For in one Spirit we were all baptized into one body—whether Jews or Greeks, whether slaves or free—and all were made to drink of one Spirit.

verses.rationale: Keeps concise correction.
verses.before: For the body does not consist of one member but of many.
verses.after: For the body is not one member but many.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the body does not consist of one member but of many.

verses.rationale: Preserves personified self-exclusion and rebuttal.
verses.before: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it any less a part of the body.
verses.after: If the foot says, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it any less part of the body.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the foot should say, “Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it any less a part of the body.

verses.rationale: Keeps deliberate parallel repetition.
verses.before: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it any less a part of the body.
verses.after: And if the ear says, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it any less part of the body.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if the ear should say, “Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body,” that does not make it any less a part of the body.

verses.rationale: Preserves sensory absurdity.
verses.before: If the whole body were an eye, where would be the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where would be the sense of smell?
verses.after: If the whole body were an eye, where would hearing be? If the whole were hearing, where would the sense of smell be?
verses.tsw_comparator: If the whole body were an eye, where would be the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where would be the sense of smell?

verses.rationale: Keeps divine placement and will.
verses.before: But as it is, God arranged the members in the body, each person of them, as he chose.
verses.after: But as it is, God arranged each one of the members in the body just as he wished.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as it is, God arranged the members in the body, each one of them, as he chose.

verses.rationale: Retains rhetorical question.
verses.before: If all were a single member, where would the body be?
verses.after: If all were one member, where would the body be?
verses.tsw_comparator: If all were a single member, where would the body be?

verses.rationale: Keeps one/many summary.
verses.before: As it is, there are many members, yet one body.
verses.after: But as it is, there are many members and one body.
verses.tsw_comparator: As it is, there are many members, yet one body.

verses.rationale: Preserves interdependence and direct speech.
verses.before: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I have no need of you,” nor again the head to the feet, “I have no need of you.”
verses.after: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I do not need you,” nor again the head to the feet, “I do not need you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The eye cannot say to the hand, “I have no need of you,” nor again the head to the feet, “I have no need of you.”

verses.rationale: Keeps perceived weakness and necessity.
verses.before: On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are necessary,
verses.after: On the contrary, the members of the body that seem weaker are indispensable,
verses.tsw_comparator: On the contrary, the members of the body that seem to be weaker are necessary,

verses.rationale: Preserves embodied social analogy and dignity.
verses.before: and those parts of the body that we think less honorable we bestow greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty,
verses.after: and those members we consider less honorable we clothe with greater honor, while our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty.
verses.tsw_comparator: and those parts of the body that we think less honorable we bestow greater honor, and our unpresentable parts are treated with greater modesty,

verses.rationale: Keeps divine rebalancing of honor.
verses.before: while our presentable parts have no need. But God has so composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,
verses.after: Our presentable parts have no need of this. But God has composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,
verses.tsw_comparator: while our presentable parts have no need. But God has so composed the body, giving greater honor to the part that lacked it,

verses.rationale: Preserves anti-division and mutual care.
verses.before: so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.
verses.after: so that there may be no division in the body but the members may have the same care for one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that there may be no division in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.

verses.rationale: Keeps shared suffering and honor.
verses.before: If one member suffers, all suffer together; if one member is honored, all rejoice together.
verses.after: If one member suffers, all the members suffer together; if one member is honored, all the members rejoice together.
verses.tsw_comparator: If one member suffers, all suffer together; if one member is honored, all rejoice together.

verses.rationale: Preserves corporate identity and individual participation.
verses.before: Now you are the body of Christ and individually members of it.
verses.after: Now you are Christ's body, and individually members of it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now you are the body of Christ and individually members of it.

verses.rationale: Keeps order and complete ministry list.
verses.before: God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then works of power, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, various kinds of tongues.
verses.after: And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then miracles, then gifts of healing, helping, leading, and various kinds of tongues.
verses.tsw_comparator: And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers, then works of power, then gifts of healings, helps, administrations, various kinds of tongues.

verses.rationale: Retains four expected-negative questions.
verses.before: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work powers?
verses.after: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work miracles?
verses.tsw_comparator: Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Do all work powers?

verses.rationale: Keeps diversity questions.
verses.before: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
verses.after: Do all have gifts of healing? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?
verses.tsw_comparator: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret?

verses.rationale: Preserves command and superlative transition.
verses.before: But earnestly desire the greater gifts. And yet I show you a still more excellent way.
verses.after: But eagerly desire the greater gifts. And now I will show you a way beyond all comparison.
verses.tsw_comparator: But earnestly desire the greater gifts. And yet I show you a still more excellent way.

verses.rationale: Keeps hypothetical extremes and noisy emptiness.
verses.before: If I speak in the tongues of mortals and of angels but do not have love, I have become a sounding gong or a clanging cymbal.
verses.after: If I speak in the tongues of humans and of angels but do not have love, I have become a resounding gong or a clashing cymbal.
verses.tsw_comparator: If I speak in the tongues of mortals and of angels but do not have love, I have become a sounding gong or a clanging cymbal.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated all and love's decisive absence.
verses.before: And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.
verses.after: And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains but do not have love, I am nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if I have prophecy and know all mysteries and all knowledge, and if I have all faith so as to move mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned boast variant and keeps total self-giving without benefit.
verses.before: And if I give away all I possess, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
verses.after: And if I give away all my possessions, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if I give away all I possess, and if I hand over my body so that I may boast, but do not have love, I gain nothing.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated love and five traits.
verses.before: Love is patient; love is kind. Love is not jealous; love does not boast; it is not arrogant.
verses.after: Love is patient; love is kind. Love does not envy, does not boast, is not puffed up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Love is patient; love is kind. Love is not jealous; love does not boast; it is not arrogant.

verses.rationale: Keeps relational behaviors and accounting image.
verses.before: It is not rude. It does not seek its own. It is not easily provoked. It does not keep account of wrong.
verses.after: It does not behave dishonorably, does not seek its own way, is not easily provoked, and does not keep an account of wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is not rude. It does not seek its own. It is not easily provoked. It does not keep account of wrong.

verses.rationale: Preserves injustice/truth contrast.
verses.before: It does not rejoice in wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth.
verses.after: It does not rejoice in injustice but rejoices together with the truth.
verses.tsw_comparator: It does not rejoice in wrongdoing, but rejoices with the truth.

verses.rationale: Keeps fourfold all refrain.
verses.before: It bears everything, believes everything, hopes everything, endures everything.
verses.after: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
verses.tsw_comparator: It bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.

verses.rationale: Preserves love's permanence and gifts' cessation.
verses.before: Love never falls. But where there are prophecies, they will be set aside; where there are tongues, they will cease; where there is knowledge, it will be set aside.
verses.after: Love never fails. But prophecies will be brought to an end, tongues will cease, and knowledge will be brought to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: Love never falls. But where there are prophecies, they will be set aside; where there are tongues, they will cease; where there is knowledge, it will be set aside.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated partiality.
verses.before: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part,
verses.after: For we know in part and we prophesy in part,
verses.tsw_comparator: For we know in part, and we prophesy in part,

verses.rationale: Uses completeness without prematurely defining the referent.
verses.before: but when the complete comes, the partial will be set aside.
verses.after: but when completeness comes, what is partial will be brought to an end.
verses.tsw_comparator: but when the complete comes, the partial will be set aside.

verses.rationale: Keeps three childhood activities and maturation.
verses.before: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I thought as a child, I reasoned as a child. When I became an adult, I set aside the things of the child.
verses.after: When I was a child, I spoke like a child, thought like a child, and reasoned like a child. When I became an adult, I put away childish things.
verses.tsw_comparator: When I was a child, I spoke as a child, I thought as a child, I reasoned as a child. When I became an adult, I set aside the things of the child.

verses.rationale: Preserves ancient mirror obscurity and knowing reciprocity.
verses.before: For now we see through a mirror, in a riddle; but then face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know fully, even as I have been fully known.
verses.after: For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face. Now I know in part; then I will know fully, just as I have been fully known.
verses.tsw_comparator: For now we see through a mirror, in a riddle; but then face to face. Now I know in part; then I shall know fully, even as I have been fully known.

verses.rationale: Keeps triad and love's primacy.
verses.before: And now faith, hope, and love remain, these three. And the greatest of these is love.
verses.after: Now faith, hope, and love remain, these three; and the greatest of these is love.
verses.tsw_comparator: And now faith, hope, and love remain, these three. And the greatest of these is love.

verses.rationale: Keeps pursuit, desire, and priority.
verses.before: Pursue love, and earnestly desire the spiritual things, but especially that you may prophesy.
verses.after: Pursue love and eagerly desire spiritual gifts, especially that you may prophesy.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pursue love, and earnestly desire the spiritual things, but especially that you may prophesy.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine address, lack of comprehension, and mysteries.
verses.before: For the one speaking in a tongue does not speak to men but to God; for no one understands, but in spirit he speaks mysteries.
verses.after: For the one who speaks in a tongue speaks not to people but to God, since no one understands; by the Spirit that person speaks mysteries.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the one speaking in a tongue does not speak to men but to God; for no one understands, but in spirit he speaks mysteries.

verses.rationale: Keeps the three communal effects.
verses.before: But the one who prophesies speaks to men for building up and encouragement and consolation.
verses.after: But the one who prophesies speaks to people for building up, encouragement, and comfort.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the one who prophesies speaks to men for building up and encouragement and consolation.

verses.rationale: Preserves self/church contrast.
verses.before: The one speaking in a tongue builds up himself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.
verses.after: The one who speaks in a tongue builds up oneself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.
verses.tsw_comparator: The one speaking in a tongue builds up himself, but the one who prophesies builds up the church.

verses.rationale: Keeps Paul's desire, ranking, exception, and purpose.
verses.before: Now I wish that you all spoke in tongues, but even more that you would prophesy; and greater is the one who prophesies than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive building up.
verses.after: Now I want all of you to speak in tongues, but even more to prophesy. The one who prophesies is greater than the one who speaks in tongues, unless someone interprets so that the church may be built up.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I wish that you all spoke in tongues, but even more that you would prophesy; and greater is the one who prophesies than the one who speaks in tongues, unless he interprets, so that the church may receive building up.

verses.rationale: Preserves question and four intelligible gifts.
verses.before: But now, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you unless I speak to you either by revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?
verses.after: Now, brothers and sisters, if I come to you speaking in tongues, how will I benefit you unless I speak to you with a revelation, knowledge, prophecy, or teaching?
verses.tsw_comparator: But now, brothers, if I come to you speaking in tongues, what will I profit you unless I speak to you either by revelation or knowledge or prophecy or teaching?

verses.rationale: Keeps musical analogy and intelligibility.
verses.before: Yet even lifeless things giving sound, whether flute or harp, if they do not give a distinction in the tones, how will it be known what is played on the flute or on the harp?
verses.after: Even lifeless instruments that produce sound, whether flute or harp, if they make no distinction between notes, how will anyone know what is played?
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet even lifeless things giving sound, whether flute or harp, if they do not give a distinction in the tones, how will it be known what is played on the flute or on the harp?

verses.rationale: Preserves military signal and consequence.
verses.before: For if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will prepare for battle?
verses.after: And if a trumpet gives an unclear sound, who will prepare for battle?
verses.tsw_comparator: For if the trumpet gives an uncertain sound, who will prepare for battle?

verses.rationale: Keeps application and air image.
verses.before: So also you, unless you give clear speech with the tongue, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into the air.
verses.after: So also with you: unless you give intelligible speech with your tongue, how will anyone know what is being said? You will simply be speaking into the air.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also you, unless you give clear speech with the tongue, how will what is spoken be known? For you will be speaking into the air.

verses.rationale: Preserves tentative expression and meaningful voices.
verses.before: There are perhaps so many kinds of languages in the world, and none is without meaning.
verses.after: There are, perhaps, many kinds of languages in the world, and none is without meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: There are perhaps so many kinds of languages in the world, and none is without meaning.

verses.rationale: Keeps reciprocal alienation.
verses.before: If then I do not know the meaning of the voice, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker a foreigner to me.
verses.after: So if I do not know the meaning of the language, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker a foreigner to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: If then I do not know the meaning of the voice, I will be a foreigner to the speaker, and the speaker a foreigner to me.

verses.rationale: Preserves zeal redirected to communal good.
verses.before: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual things, seek that you may abound for the building up of the church.
verses.after: So also with you: since you are eager for spiritual manifestations, seek to excel in building up the church.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also you, since you are zealous for spiritual things, seek that you may abound for the building up of the church.

verses.rationale: Keeps speaker's responsibility.
verses.before: So let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.
verses.after: Therefore, the one who speaks in a tongue should pray to interpret.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore let the one who speaks in a tongue pray that he may interpret.

verses.rationale: Preserves spirit/mind contrast.
verses.before: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
verses.after: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if I pray in a tongue, my spirit prays, but my mind is unfruitful.

verses.rationale: Keeps both paired resolutions.
verses.before: What then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will also sing with the mind.
verses.after: What then? I will pray with the spirit, but I will also pray with the mind. I will sing praise with the spirit, but I will also sing praise with the mind.
verses.tsw_comparator: What then? I will pray with the spirit, and I will also pray with the mind; I will sing with the spirit, and I will also sing with the mind.

verses.rationale: Preserves outsider, Amen, and comprehension issue.
verses.before: Otherwise, if you bless in spirit, how will the one occupying the place of the uninstructed say “Amen” at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?
verses.after: Otherwise, if you offer praise by the spirit, how can someone in the place of an outsider say “Amen” to your thanksgiving, since that person does not know what you are saying?
verses.tsw_comparator: Otherwise, if you bless in spirit, how will the one occupying the place of the uninstructed say “Amen” at your thanksgiving, since he does not know what you are saying?

verses.rationale: Keeps personal validity and communal failure.
verses.before: For you give thanks well enough, but the other is not built up.
verses.after: You may be giving thanks well enough, but the other person is not built up.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you give thanks well enough, but the other is not built up.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's own practice.
verses.before: I thank God, I speak in tongues more than all of you;
verses.after: I thank God that I speak in tongues more than all of you.
verses.tsw_comparator: I thank God, I speak in tongues more than all of you;

verses.rationale: Keeps exact numbers and priority.
verses.before: but in the church I prefer to speak five words with my mind so that I may instruct others also, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.
verses.after: But in church I would rather speak five intelligible words to instruct others than ten thousand words in a tongue.
verses.tsw_comparator: but in the church I prefer to speak five words with my mind so that I may instruct others also, rather than ten thousand words in a tongue.

verses.rationale: Preserves child/infant/adult contrasts.
verses.before: Brothers, do not be children in your thinking; yet in evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.
verses.after: Brothers and sisters, do not be children in your thinking. Be infants in evil, but mature in your thinking.
verses.tsw_comparator: Brothers, do not be children in your thinking; yet in evil be infants, but in your thinking be mature.

verses.rationale: Keeps foreign speech and refused hearing.
verses.before: In the law it is written, “By people of other tongues and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to me,” says the Lord.
verses.after: In the law it is written: “By people of other tongues and by the lips of foreigners I will speak to this people, yet even then they will not listen to me,” says the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the law it is written, “By people of other tongues and by the lips of strangers I will speak to this people, and even so they will not listen to me,” says the Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves Paul's stated audience contrast.
verses.before: So then tongues are for a sign, not to believers but to unbelievers; but prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
verses.after: So tongues are a sign not for believers but for unbelievers, while prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.
verses.tsw_comparator: So then tongues are for a sign, not to believers but to unbelievers; but prophecy is not for unbelievers but for believers.

verses.rationale: Keeps whole assembly and visitor reaction.
verses.before: So if the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and uninstructed or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your mind?
verses.after: Therefore, if the whole church gathers together and everyone speaks in tongues, and outsiders or unbelievers enter, will they not say you are out of your minds?
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore if the whole church comes together and all speak in tongues, and uninstructed or unbelievers enter, will they not say that you are out of your mind?

verses.rationale: Preserves communal exposure and examination.
verses.before: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or uninstructed person enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all;
verses.after: But if everyone prophesies and an unbeliever or outsider enters, that person is convicted by everyone and called to account by everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or uninstructed person enters, he is convicted by all, he is called to account by all;

verses.rationale: Keeps disclosure, bodily worship, and confession.
verses.before: the secrets of his heart become manifest; and so falling on his face he will worship God, declaring that God is truly among you.
verses.after: The secrets of that person's heart become evident, and so, falling facedown, the person will worship God and declare, “God is truly among you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: the secrets of his heart become manifest; and so falling on his face he will worship God, declaring that God is truly among you.

verses.rationale: Preserves participatory variety and governing purpose.
verses.before: What then, brothers and sisters? When you come together, each has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let everything be done for building up.
verses.after: What then, brothers and sisters? When you gather, each one has a psalm, a teaching, a revelation, a tongue, or an interpretation. Let everything be done for building up.
verses.tsw_comparator: What then, brothers? When you come together, each has a psalm, has a teaching, has a revelation, has a tongue, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for building up.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact limits, sequence, and interpretation.
verses.before: If someone speaks in a tongue, let it be by two or at most three, and in turn, and let one interpret;
verses.after: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be two, or at most three, each in turn, and let one person interpret.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let it be by two or at most three, and in turn, and let one interpret;

verses.rationale: Preserves conditional silence and private speech.
verses.before: but if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the church and speak to himself and to God.
verses.after: But if there is no interpreter, the speaker should remain silent in church and speak to oneself and to God.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in the church and speak to himself and to God.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact limits and communal evaluation.
verses.before: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern;
verses.after: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern what is said.
verses.tsw_comparator: And let two or three prophets speak, and let the others discern;

verses.rationale: Preserves orderly yielding.
verses.before: but if something is revealed to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.
verses.after: But if a revelation comes to another person who is seated, the first speaker should be silent.
verses.tsw_comparator: but if something is revealed to another sitting by, let the first keep silent.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal participation with order and purpose.
verses.before: For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged;
verses.after: For you can all prophesy one by one, so that everyone may learn and everyone may be encouraged.
verses.tsw_comparator: For you can all prophesy one by one, so that all may learn and all may be encouraged;

verses.rationale: Preserves self-governed prophetic agency.
verses.before: and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
verses.after: And prophets' spirits are subject to prophets,
verses.tsw_comparator: and the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.

verses.rationale: Keeps theological ground and broad church frame.
verses.before: For God is not a God of disorder but of peace. As in all the churches of the holy ones,
verses.after: for God is not a God of disorder but of peace, as in all the churches of the saints. As in all the churches of the holy ones,
verses.tsw_comparator: For God is not a God of disorder but of peace. As in all the churches of the holy ones,

verses.rationale: Translates the pinned instruction directly without erasing tension with 11:5.
verses.before: let the women keep silent in the churches; for they are not permitted to speak, but let them be in submission, as also the law says.
verses.after: Women should remain silent in the churches, for they are not permitted to speak but should be in submission, as the law also says.
verses.tsw_comparator: let the women keep silent in the churches; for they are not permitted to speak, but let them be in submission, as also the law says.

verses.rationale: Retains marriage-specific direction and shame language.
verses.before: And if they desire to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
verses.after: If they want to learn something, they should ask their own husbands at home, for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if they desire to learn anything, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for a woman to speak in church.

verses.rationale: Keeps two rebuking questions.
verses.before: Or did the word of God go out from you, or did it come to you only?
verses.after: Or did God's word originate with you? Or did it reach only you?
verses.tsw_comparator: Or did the word of God go out from you, or did it come to you only?

verses.rationale: Preserves claimed authority and discernment test.
verses.before: If someone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things I write to you are a command of the Lord.
verses.after: If anyone thinks they are a prophet or spiritual, that person should recognize that what I write to you is the Lord's command.
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone thinks he is a prophet or spiritual, let him acknowledge that the things I write to you are a command of the Lord.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned passive reading and reciprocal wordplay.
