verses.before: But if someone ignores this, he is ignored.
verses.after: But if anyone refuses to recognize this, that person is not recognized.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if anyone ignores this, he is ignored.

verses.rationale: Keeps positive desire and negative prohibition.
verses.before: So, my brothers and sisters, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
verses.after: So then, my brothers and sisters, eagerly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, my brothers, earnestly desire to prophesy, and do not forbid speaking in tongues.

verses.rationale: Preserves comprehensive concluding rule.
verses.before: But let everything be done properly and in order.
verses.after: But let everything be done properly and in an orderly way.
verses.tsw_comparator: But let all things be done properly and in order.

verses.rationale: Keeps proclamation, reception, and standing.
verses.before: Now I reveal to you, brothers and sisters, the good news which I proclaimed to you, which also you received, in which also you stand,
verses.after: Now I remind you, brothers and sisters, of the good news I proclaimed to you, which you also received and in which you stand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I make known to you, brothers, the gospel which I proclaimed to you, which also you received, in which also you stand,

verses.rationale: Preserves ongoing salvation, condition, and empty-faith possibility.
verses.before: through which also you are being saved, if you hold firmly to the word I proclaimed to you—unless you believed in vain.
verses.after: Through it you are also being saved, if you hold firmly to the message I proclaimed to you—unless you believed for nothing.
verses.tsw_comparator: through which also you are being saved, if you hold fast to the word I proclaimed to you—unless you believed in vain.

verses.rationale: Keeps transmission, priority, death, and scriptural accordance.
verses.before: For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
verses.after: For I handed on to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
verses.tsw_comparator: For I delivered to you as of first importance what I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,

verses.rationale: Preserves burial, enduring resurrection result, timing, and Scripture.
verses.before: and that he was buried, and that he has been raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
verses.after: that he was buried, that he has been raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,
verses.tsw_comparator: and that he was buried, and that he has been raised on the third day according to the Scriptures,

verses.rationale: Keeps named and group witnesses.
verses.before: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve;
verses.after: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the Twelve.
verses.tsw_comparator: and that he appeared to Cephas, then to the twelve;

verses.rationale: Preserves number, contemporaneous witnesses, and death euphemism.
verses.before: then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at one time, most of whom remain until now, though some have fallen asleep;
verses.after: Then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers and sisters at one time, most of whom remain alive until now, though some have fallen asleep in death.
verses.tsw_comparator: then he appeared to more than five hundred brothers at one time, most of whom remain until now, though some have fallen asleep;

verses.rationale: Keeps ordered appearances.
verses.before: then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles;
verses.after: Then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles.
verses.tsw_comparator: then he appeared to James, then to all the apostles;

verses.rationale: Retains Paul's harsh birth image.
verses.before: and last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me.
verses.after: Last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me.
verses.tsw_comparator: and last of all, as to one untimely born, he appeared also to me.

verses.rationale: Keeps self-abasement and reason.
verses.before: For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
verses.after: For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted God's church.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I am the least of the apostles, unworthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.

verses.rationale: Preserves grace/empty wordplay and labor qualification.
verses.before: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain; but I labored more abundantly than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God with me.
verses.after: But by God's grace I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not empty. Instead, I worked harder than all of them—yet not I, but God's grace with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me was not in vain; but I labored more abundantly than all of them—yet not I, but the grace of God with me.

verses.rationale: Keeps unified apostolic message.
verses.before: So whether it was I or they, so we proclaim and so you believed.
verses.after: Whether, then, it was I or they, this is what we proclaim, and this is what you believed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore whether it was I or they, so we proclaim and so you believed.

verses.rationale: Preserves internal contradiction question.
verses.before: Now if Christ is proclaimed as having been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
verses.after: Now if Christ is proclaimed as raised from the dead, how can some among you say there is no resurrection of the dead?
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if Christ is proclaimed as having been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?

verses.rationale: Keeps first logical consequence.
verses.before: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised;
verses.after: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, then not even Christ has been raised.
verses.tsw_comparator: But if there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ been raised;

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated emptiness.
verses.before: and if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your trust is empty.
verses.after: And if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your faith is empty.
verses.tsw_comparator: and if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is empty, and your faith is empty.

verses.rationale: Keeps grave false-witness consequence.
verses.before: Moreover we are even found to be false witnesses of God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if indeed the dead are not raised.
verses.after: We are also found to be false witnesses about God, because we testified about God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if it is true that the dead are not raised.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover we are even found to be false witnesses of God, because we testified against God that he raised Christ, whom he did not raise if indeed the dead are not raised.

verses.rationale: Retains deliberate repetition.
verses.before: For if the dead are not raised, neither has Christ been raised;
verses.after: For if the dead are not raised, not even Christ has been raised.
verses.tsw_comparator: For if the dead are not raised, neither has Christ been raised;

verses.rationale: Keeps spiritual consequence.
verses.before: and if Christ has not been raised, your trust is futile; you are still in your sins.
verses.after: And if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.
verses.tsw_comparator: and if Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins.

verses.rationale: Preserves death euphemism and stark loss.
verses.before: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
verses.after: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then those also who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished.

verses.rationale: Keeps limited-horizon consequence.
verses.before: If in this life only we have hoped in Christ, we are of all people most to be pitied.
verses.after: If we have placed our hope in Christ only for this life, we are more pitiful than all people.
verses.tsw_comparator: If in this life only we have hoped in Christ, we are of all people most to be pitied.

verses.rationale: Preserves triumphant turn and harvest image.
verses.before: But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of people who have fallen asleep.
verses.after: But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now Christ has been raised from the dead, the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep.

verses.rationale: Keeps human mediation parallel.
verses.before: For since through a man came death, through a man also came resurrection of the dead.
verses.after: For since death came through a human being, resurrection of the dead also comes through a human being.
verses.tsw_comparator: For since through a man came death, through a man also came resurrection of the dead.

verses.rationale: Preserves both occurrences of all and corporate spheres.
verses.before: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
verses.after: For just as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: For as in Adam all die, so also in Christ all will be made alive.

verses.rationale: Keeps sequence and coming.
verses.before: But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then people who are Christ’s at his coming,
verses.after: But each in proper order: Christ the firstfruits, then at his coming those who belong to Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: But each in his own order: Christ the firstfruits, then those who are Christ’s at his coming,

verses.rationale: Preserves transfer of kingdom and defeated powers.
verses.before: then the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he abolishes all rule and all authority and power.
verses.after: Then comes the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, after he brings to an end every ruler and every authority and power.
verses.tsw_comparator: then the end, when he hands over the kingdom to God the Father, when he abolishes all rule and all authority and power.

verses.rationale: Keeps necessary reign and subjugation image.
verses.before: For he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet.
verses.after: For he must reign until he puts all his enemies under his feet.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he must reign until he has put all enemies under his feet.

verses.rationale: Preserves death as enemy and final defeat.
verses.before: The last enemy to be abolished is death.
verses.after: The last enemy to be abolished is death.
verses.tsw_comparator: The last enemy to be abolished is death.

verses.rationale: Keeps quotation, all, and stated exception.
verses.before: For “he has put everything in subjection under his feet.” But when it says “everything are put in subjection,” it is evident that it excludes the one who subjected everything to him.
verses.after: For “he subjected all things under his feet.” But when it says all things are subjected, it is clear that this excludes the one who subjected all things to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: For “he has put all things in subjection under his feet.” But when it says “all things are put in subjection,” it is evident that it excludes the one who subjected all things to him.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated subjection and final purpose.
verses.before: And when everything are subjected to him, then the Son himself also will be subjected to the one who subjected everything to him, so that God may be all in all.
verses.after: And when all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself will also be subjected to the one who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when all things are subjected to him, then the Son himself also will be subjected to the one who subjected all things to him, so that God may be all in all.

verses.rationale: Keeps disputed practice without explaining or endorsing it.
verses.before: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized on behalf of them?
verses.after: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized for the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why are people baptized for them?
verses.tsw_comparator: Otherwise, what will those do who are baptized on behalf of the dead? If the dead are not raised at all, why then are they baptized on behalf of them?

verses.rationale: Preserves ongoing apostolic danger.
verses.before: Why also are we in danger every hour?
verses.after: And why are we in danger every hour?
verses.tsw_comparator: Why also are we in danger every hour?

verses.rationale: Keeps daily death and emphatic oath.
verses.before: I die daily—I affirm it, brothers and sisters, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.after: I die every day—I swear by my pride in you, brothers and sisters, which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: I die daily—I affirm it, brothers, by the boasting in you which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord.

verses.rationale: Preserves possible metaphor, geography, and quotation.
verses.before: If according to man I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
verses.after: If I fought wild beasts in Ephesus merely as a human, what did I gain? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If according to man I fought with beasts at Ephesus, what does it profit me? If the dead are not raised, “Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die.”

verses.rationale: Keeps warning and proverbial citation.
verses.before: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good morals.”
verses.after: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good character.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be deceived: “Bad company corrupts good morals.”

verses.rationale: Preserves awakening, command, ignorance, and shame.
verses.before: Become sober as you ought, and do not sin; for some have no knowledge of God. I speak to your shame.
verses.after: Come back to your senses as you ought, and stop sinning, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: Become sober as you ought, and do not sin; for some have no knowledge of God. I speak to your shame.

verses.rationale: Keeps both bodily resurrection questions.
verses.before: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?”
verses.after: But someone will ask, “How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But someone will say, “How are the dead raised? And with what kind of body do they come?”

verses.rationale: Retains insult and seed-death analogy.
verses.before: Foolish one! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
verses.after: Foolish person! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Foolish one! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.

verses.rationale: Keeps continuity and difference in seed image.
verses.before: And what you sow, you do not sow the body that will be, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or of some other grain;
verses.after: And what you sow is not the body that will be, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or some other grain.
verses.tsw_comparator: And what you sow, you do not sow the body that will be, but a bare seed, perhaps of wheat or of some other grain;

verses.rationale: Preserves divine choice and particularity.
verses.before: but God gives it a body as he willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.
verses.after: But God gives it a body as he has chosen, and to each kind of seed its own body.
verses.tsw_comparator: but God gives it a body as he willed, and to each of the seeds its own body.

verses.rationale: Keeps four embodied kinds.
verses.before: Not all flesh is the same flesh, but one of humans, another flesh of animals, another of birds, and another of fish.
verses.after: Not all flesh is the same: humans have one kind, land animals another, birds another, and fish another.
verses.tsw_comparator: Not all flesh is the same flesh, but one of humans, another flesh of animals, another of birds, and another of fish.

verses.rationale: Preserves body and differing glory.
verses.before: And there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is one, and the glory of the earthly is another.
verses.after: There are also heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is one kind and that of the earthly another.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there are heavenly bodies and earthly bodies, but the glory of the heavenly is one, and the glory of the earthly is another.

verses.rationale: Keeps celestial distinctions and repetition.
verses.before: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory.
verses.after: The sun has one glory, the moon another, and the stars another; indeed, star differs from star in glory.
verses.tsw_comparator: There is one glory of the sun, and another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for star differs from star in glory.

verses.rationale: Begins the repeated sow/raise contrasts.
verses.before: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption.
verses.after: So also is the resurrection of the dead: what is sown perishable is raised imperishable;
verses.tsw_comparator: So also is the resurrection of the dead. It is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption.

verses.rationale: Keeps two parallel transformations.
verses.before: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
verses.after: it is sown in dishonor and raised in glory; it is sown in weakness and raised in power;
verses.tsw_comparator: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.

verses.rationale: Preserves body in both states and explicit inference.
verses.before: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual.
verses.after: it is sown a natural body and raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual body.
verses.tsw_comparator: It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body. If there is a natural body, there is also a spiritual.

verses.rationale: Keeps Adam contrast and Spirit title.
verses.before: So also it is written, “The first man Adam became a living soul”; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.
verses.after: So it is written: “The first human, Adam, became a living being”; the last Adam became a life-giving Spirit.
verses.tsw_comparator: So also it is written, “The first man Adam became a living soul”; the last Adam became a life-giving spirit.

verses.rationale: Preserves sequence.
verses.before: However, the spiritual is not first, but the natural, then the spiritual.
verses.after: But the spiritual did not come first; the natural did, and then the spiritual.
verses.tsw_comparator: However, the spiritual is not first, but the natural, then the spiritual.

verses.rationale: Keeps origins and earthy material.
verses.before: The first man is from the earth, earthy; the second man is from heaven.
verses.after: The first human was from the earth, made of dust; the second human is from heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first man is from the earth, earthy; the second man is from heaven.

verses.rationale: Preserves two representative solidarities.
verses.before: As is the earthy, such also are the earthy; and as is the heavenly, such also are the heavenly.
verses.after: As was the one made of dust, so are those made of dust; and as is the heavenly one, so are those who are heavenly.
verses.tsw_comparator: As is the earthy, such also are the earthy; and as is the heavenly, such also are the heavenly.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned future and image transformation.
verses.before: And just as we have borne the image of the earthy, we will also bear the image of the heavenly.
verses.after: And just as we have borne the image of the one made of dust, we will also bear the image of the heavenly one.
verses.tsw_comparator: And just as we have borne the image of the earthy, we will also bear the image of the heavenly.

verses.rationale: Keeps inheritance incapacity and corruption contrast.
verses.before: Now this I say, brothers and sisters, that flesh and blood are not able to inherit the kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.
verses.after: Now I say this, brothers and sisters: flesh and blood cannot inherit God's kingdom, nor does the perishable inherit the imperishable.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now this I say, brothers, that flesh and blood are not able to inherit the kingdom of God, nor does corruption inherit incorruption.

verses.rationale: Preserves pinned negation placement and universal change.
verses.before: Look, I tell you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,
verses.after: Look, I tell you a mystery: we will not all fall asleep, but we will all be changed,
verses.tsw_comparator: Behold, I tell you a mystery: we will not all sleep, but we will all be changed,

verses.rationale: Keeps speed, signal, resurrection, and transformation.
verses.before: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.
verses.after: in an instant, in the blink of an eye, at the last trumpet. For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed.
verses.tsw_comparator: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we will be changed.

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing metaphor and paired states.
verses.before: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.
verses.after: For this perishable body must put on imperishability, and this mortal body must put on immortality.
verses.tsw_comparator: For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality.

verses.rationale: Keeps fulfillment and swallowed-death image.
verses.before: But when this corruptible puts on incorruption, and this mortal puts on immortality, then will come about the word that is written: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.
verses.after: And when this perishable body puts on imperishability and this mortal body puts on immortality, then the written saying will come true: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But when this corruptible puts on incorruption, and this mortal puts on immortality, then will come about the word that is written: “Death has been swallowed up in victory.

verses.rationale: Preserves direct taunt and pinned repeated death.
verses.before: O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?”
verses.after: “Where, death, is your victory? Where, death, is your sting?”
verses.tsw_comparator: O death, where is your victory? O death, where is your sting?”

verses.rationale: Keeps terse causal definitions.
verses.before: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law;
verses.after: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law;

verses.rationale: Preserves thanksgiving and divine gift.
verses.before: but thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.after: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.tsw_comparator: but thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

verses.rationale: Keeps commands, abundance, and nonempty labor.
verses.before: So, my beloved brothers and sisters, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
verses.after: Therefore, my beloved brothers and sisters, be steadfast and immovable, always excelling in the Lord's work, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not empty.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.

verses.rationale: Preserves collection, recipients, and shared instruction.
verses.before: Now concerning the collection for the holy ones: as I directed the churches of Galatia, so also you are to do.
verses.after: Now concerning the collection for the saints: do as I directed the churches of Galatia.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now concerning the collection for the holy ones: as I directed the churches of Galatia, so also you are to do.

verses.rationale: Keeps weekly individual saving and proportional means.
verses.before: On the first day of every week, each person of you is to put something aside, storing up as he may prosper, so that no collections be made when I come.
verses.after: On the first day of every week, each of you should set something aside and save it, in keeping with whatever prosperity you have, so that collections will not be made when I come.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the first day of every week, each one of you is to put something aside, storing up as he may prosper, so that no collections be made when I come.

verses.rationale: Preserves community-approved couriers and gift destination.
verses.before: And when I arrive, whomever you approve, I will send with letters to carry your gift to Jerusalem;
verses.after: Then when I arrive, I will send those you approve with letters to carry your gracious gift to Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when I arrive, whomever you approve, I will send with letters to carry your gift to Jerusalem;

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional travel and companions.
verses.before: and if it is fitting for me also to go, they will go with me.
verses.after: And if it is appropriate for me to go as well, they will go with me.
verses.tsw_comparator: and if it is fitting for me also to go, they will go with me.

verses.rationale: Preserves itinerary and repetition.
verses.before: Yet I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia;
verses.after: I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia.
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will come to you after I pass through Macedonia, for I am passing through Macedonia;

verses.rationale: Keeps tentative stay and community support.
verses.before: and perhaps I will stay with you or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I go.
verses.after: Perhaps I will stay with you or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I go.
verses.tsw_comparator: and perhaps I will stay with you or even spend the winter, so that you may send me on my way wherever I go.

verses.rationale: Preserves relational desire and divine contingency.
verses.before: For I do not want to see you now just in passing, for I hope to remain with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
verses.after: For I do not want to see you now only in passing. I hope to remain with you for some time, if the Lord permits.
verses.tsw_comparator: For I do not want to see you now just in passing, for I hope to remain with you for some time, if the Lord permits.

verses.rationale: Keeps place and festival timeline.
verses.before: Yet I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,
verses.after: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,
verses.tsw_comparator: But I will remain in Ephesus until Pentecost,

verses.rationale: Preserves opportunity and opposition together.
verses.before: for a wide door has opened for me for effective work, and there are many adversaries.
verses.after: for a great and effective door has opened for me, and there are many opponents.
verses.tsw_comparator: for a wide door has opened for me for effective work, and there are many adversaries.

verses.rationale: Keeps protection and equal work.
verses.before: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he is doing the work of the Lord, as I also am;
verses.after: If Timothy comes, see that he has no reason to be afraid while among you, for he is doing the Lord's work, just as I am.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now if Timothy comes, see that he is with you without fear, for he is doing the work of the Lord, as I also am;

verses.rationale: Preserves warning, support, and expected party.
verses.before: so let no one despise him. But send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers and sisters.
verses.after: So no one should despise him. Send him on his way in peace so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: so let no one despise him. But send him on his way in peace, so that he may come to me, for I am expecting him with the brothers.

verses.rationale: Keeps Apollos's independent refusal and future openness.
verses.before: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers and sisters; but it was not at all his will to come now, but he will come when he has opportunity.
verses.after: Now concerning our brother Apollos: I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers, but it was not at all his will to come now. He will come when he has an opportunity.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now concerning Apollos the brother, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brothers; but it was not at all his will to come now, but he will come when he has opportunity.

verses.rationale: Retains four terse imperatives and gendered idiom's courage sense.
verses.before: Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong.
verses.after: Stay alert; stand firm in the faith; be courageous; be strong.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong.

verses.rationale: Keeps comprehensive love rule.
verses.before: Let all that you do be done in love.
verses.after: Let everything you do be done in love.
verses.tsw_comparator: Let all that you do be done in love.

verses.rationale: Preserves household, geography, self-devotion, and continuing appeal.
verses.before: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters—you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have devoted themselves to service for the holy ones—
verses.after: Now I urge you, brothers and sisters—you know the household of Stephanas, that they are the firstfruits of Achaia and have devoted themselves to serving the saints—
verses.tsw_comparator: Now I urge you, brothers—you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the firstfruits of Achaia, and that they have devoted themselves to service for the holy ones—

verses.rationale: Keeps submission to laboring servants.
verses.before: that you also be subject to such people and to everyone who works and labors with them.
verses.after: submit yourselves to such people and to everyone who works and labors with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: that you also be subject to such people and to everyone who works and labors with them.

verses.rationale: Names all three and their representative provision.
verses.before: I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because they have supplied what was lacking on your part.
verses.after: I rejoice at the arrival of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because they supplied what was lacking from you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas and Fortunatus and Achaicus, because they have supplied what was lacking on your part.

verses.rationale: Keeps mutual refreshment and recognition.
verses.before: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge such men.
verses.after: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore, recognize such people.
verses.tsw_comparator: For they refreshed my spirit and yours. Therefore acknowledge such men.

verses.rationale: Preserves regional churches, names, house church, and warmth.
verses.before: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the church in their house.
verses.after: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca, together with the church in their house, greet you warmly in the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: The churches of Asia greet you. Aquila and Prisca greet you warmly in the Lord, together with the church in their house.

verses.rationale: Keeps universal greeting and embodied response.
verses.before: All the brothers and sisters greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
verses.after: All the brothers and sisters greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the brothers greet you. Greet one another with a holy kiss.

verses.rationale: Preserves autograph identification.
verses.before: The greeting is in my own hand—Paul.
verses.after: I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: The greeting is in my own hand—Paul.

verses.rationale: Retains curse and untranslated Aramaic plea.
verses.before: If someone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come!
verses.after: If anyone does not love the Lord, let that person be accursed. Marana tha!
verses.tsw_comparator: If anyone does not love the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come!

verses.rationale: Keeps brief benediction.
verses.before: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.after: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you.

verses.rationale: Preserves personal love and inclusive all.
verses.before: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
verses.after: My love be with all of you in Christ Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
